**Domenico Modugno** (born January 9, 1928 – died August 6, 1994) was a famous Italian singer, songwriter, and actor. Later in his life, he also became a member of the [Italian Parliament](link_14). He is best known for his huge international hit song from 1958, "Nel blu dipinto di blu" (often called "Volare"). This song won him two [Grammy Awards](link_15). Many people see him as the first true Italian _cantautore_, which means a singer-songwriter who writes and performs their own songs.

## Domenico Modugno's Early Life

Domenico Modugno was born in [Polignano a Mare](link_5), Italy, on January 9, 1928. He was the youngest of four children. His father, Vito Cosimo Modugno, worked as a police commander, and his mother, Pasqua Lorusso, was a housewife.

When Domenico was nine, his family moved to San Pietro Vernotico. There, he went to primary school and learned the local dialect. He later attended secondary school in Lecce.

## Domenico Modugno's Music Career

While still a student, Domenico Modugno started acting in films. His first taste of fame came in 1957 when his song "Lazzarella" placed second in a big Italian music contest called the Festival della Canzone Napoletana.

The biggest moment of his career happened in 1958. He entered the Sanremo Music Festival with a song he co-wrote called "Nel blu dipinto di blu". This song won the contest and became a massive hit all over the world. It sold over 22 million copies and won two [Grammy Awards](link_15). The song also represented Italy in the 1958 Eurovision Song Contest, where it finished third.

[![Image 5: Eurovision Song Contest 1958 - Domenico Modugno](https://kids.kiddle.co/images/thumb/7/7f/Eurovision_Song_Contest_1958_-_Domenico_Modugno.png/300px-Eurovision_Song_Contest_1958_-_Domenico_Modugno.png)](https://kids.kiddle.co/Image:Eurovision_Song_Contest_1958_-_Domenico_Modugno.png)

[](https://kids.kiddle.co/Image:Eurovision_Song_Contest_1958_-_Domenico_Modugno.png "Enlarge")

 Domenico Modugno singing "Nel blu, dipinto di blu" at the Eurovision Song Contest 1958.

Modugno won the Sanremo Music Festival again in 1959 with "Piove" (also known as "Ciao, ciao bambina"). He also came in second place in 1960 with "Libero." He represented Italy in the Eurovision Song Contest again in 1959. Later, his song "Io" was covered by [Elvis Presley](link_16) in English, titled "Ask Me."

In 1962, Modugno won the Sanremo Music Festival for a third time with "Addio... addio...." He returned to Eurovision in 1966 with "Dio, come ti amo." Other artists like [Sergio Franchi](link_17) and Jack Jones later recorded this song.

Besides singing, Modugno acted in many movies, appearing in 44 films. He also produced two films, including _Tutto è musica_ (1963), which was about his own life. In the 1970s, he started focusing more on classical music and acting in modern operas.

## Domenico Modugno's Later Years

In 1984, Domenico Modugno had a serious health issue that affected his ability to perform. This led him to focus on his recovery.

From 1986, he became very active in fighting for the rights of people with disabilities. In June 1987, he was elected to the Italian Parliament as a representative for [Turin](link_13). He was part of the Radical Party, a group focused on social issues. He spoke out against unfair treatment of patients in hospitals and supported campaigns for human rights.

Modugno returned to music in 1992–1993. His last song was "Delfini" (meaning "Dolphins"), which he sang with his son, Massimo, in 1993.

Domenico Modugno passed away on August 6, 1994, at the age of 66. He died from a heart attack at his home on the island of [Lampedusa](link_7), south of Sicily. His beautiful beach house was later put up for sale.

## [Trivia](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0197931/bio/#trivia)

*   While Dalida was professionally very successful, her private life was marred by a series of failed relationships and personal problems. In January 1967, Dalida took part in the Sanremo Festival with her new lover, Italian singer, songwriter and actor [Luigi Tenco](link_55). The song he presented was "Ciao amore ciao" ("Bye Love, Bye"), which he sang together with Dalida. But stressed, Tenco failed despite Dalida's performance. Tenco committed suicide on 27 January 1967, after learning that his song had been eliminated from the final competition. Tenco was found by Dalida in his hotel room with a bullet wound in his left temple and a note announcing that his gesture was against the jury and public's choices during the competition. In September 1970 her former husband (1956-1961) [Lucien Morisse](link_56), with whom she was on good terms, committed suicide, shooting himself in the head. In April 1975, her close friend singer [Mike Brant](link_57) leapt to his death from an apartment in Paris. He was 28. In July 1983, her lover from 1972 to 1981, [Richard Chanfray](link_58), committed suicide by inhaling the exhaust gas of his Renault 25 car.   
*   She recorded 500 French songs, 200 of which were translated into Italian, and 200 into other languages. She sold more than 80 million records world-wide.   
*   In 1967 her lover, singer [Luigi Tenco](link_55), took his own life. She discovered his dead body. She herself attempted suicide a few days later.   
*   Had been [Richard Chanfray](link_58)'s lover for 9 years. He committed suicide in 1983, three years after they broke up.   
*   She's portrayed by [Sabrina Ferilli](link_59) in [Dalida (2005)](link_60).

**Polignano a Mare** is a beautiful town in southern [Italy](link_6). It's located right on the [Adriatic Sea](link_17) in a region called [Apulia](link_8). This town is famous for its stunning cliffs and sea caves. People in Polignano a Mare mainly earn a living from tourism, farming, and fishing. It's a popular spot for visitors from all over the world.

## Contents

*   [History of Polignano a Mare](https://kids.kiddle.co/Polignano_a_Mare#History_of_Polignano_a_Mare)
    *   [Ancient Beginnings](https://kids.kiddle.co/Polignano_a_Mare#Ancient_Beginnings)
    *   [A Center for Trade](https://kids.kiddle.co/Polignano_a_Mare#A_Center_for_Trade)
    *   [Foreign Rule and Growth](https://kids.kiddle.co/Polignano_a_Mare#Foreign_Rule_and_Growth)
    *   [Protecting the Town](https://kids.kiddle.co/Polignano_a_Mare#Protecting_the_Town)

*   [Famous Landmarks to See](https://kids.kiddle.co/Polignano_a_Mare#Famous_Landmarks_to_See)
*   [Getting Around Polignano a Mare](https://kids.kiddle.co/Polignano_a_Mare#Getting_Around_Polignano_a_Mare)
*   [Twin Towns](https://kids.kiddle.co/Polignano_a_Mare#Twin_Towns)
*   [See also](https://kids.kiddle.co/Polignano_a_Mare#See_also)

## History of Polignano a Mare

### Ancient Beginnings

People have lived in the area around Polignano a Mare for a very long time. Archeologists have found old remains in a place called Santa Barbara. Many believe this was once an ancient Greek city named _Neapolis_.

Some historians think that [Dionysius II of Syracuse](link_18) founded this city in the 4th century BC. Other stories suggest that [Julius Caesar](link_19) might have founded Polignano a Mare. It was an important stop along an old Roman road called the Via Traiana.

### A Center for Trade

Because of its great location on the Adriatic Sea, Polignano a Mare quickly became a busy trading center. Ships would come and go, bringing goods from different places. This helped the town grow and become well-known.

### Foreign Rule and Growth

Different empires and kingdoms ruled Polignano a Mare over the centuries, each helping it develop. In the 6th century, the [Byzantine Empire](link_20) helped organize the town's government.

Later, in the 11th century, the Normans took over. They helped the local economy by boosting the production of olive oil. This made the town's economy stronger.

### Protecting the Town

The Angioinians, another ruling family, built strong defenses around the town. These fortifications protected Polignano a Mare from dangers like the Turkish army and various illnesses.

Under the [Aragonese crown](link_21), Polignano a Mare reached its best time. Both its economy and culture thrived. Business people and traders from all over the world came to meet and trade here.

## Famous Landmarks to See

Polignano a Mare has many interesting places to visit. Here are some of them:

*   Fondazione Museo "Pino Pascali"
*   Palazzo dell'Orologio (Clock Palace)
*   Abbey of San Vito Martire
*   Church of Santa Maria Assunta
*   The Grotta Palazzese Hotel
*   Lama Monachile [![Image 5: Lama Monachile Arpa 2022](https://kids.kiddle.co/images/thumb/5/57/Lama_Monachile_Arpa_2022.jpg/300px-Lama_Monachile_Arpa_2022.jpg)](https://kids.kiddle.co/Image:Lama_Monachile_Arpa_2022.jpg)[](https://kids.kiddle.co/Image:Lama_Monachile_Arpa_2022.jpg "Enlarge")  Lama Monachile is a famous beach nestled between cliffs.   

## Getting Around Polignano a Mare

The town has its own train station, called Polignano a Mare railway station. This makes it easy for people to travel to and from Polignano a Mare by train.

## Twin Towns

Polignano a Mare has special friendships with other towns. These are called "twin towns":

*   [![Image 6: Italy](https://kids.kiddle.co/images/thumb/0/03/Flag_of_Italy.svg/23px-Flag_of_Italy.svg.png)](https://kids.kiddle.co/Italy [link_6] "Italy") San Miniato, Italy

# Trivia

## Dalida

Edit

*   While Dalida was professionally very successful, her private life was marred by a series of failed relationships and personal problems. In January 1967, Dalida took part in the Sanremo Festival with her new lover, Italian singer, songwriter and actor [Luigi Tenco](link_49). The song he presented was "Ciao amore ciao" ("Bye Love, Bye"), which he sang together with Dalida. But stressed, Tenco failed despite Dalida's performance. Tenco committed suicide on 27 January 1967, after learning that his song had been eliminated from the final competition. Tenco was found by Dalida in his hotel room with a bullet wound in his left temple and a note announcing that his gesture was against the jury and public's choices during the competition. In September 1970 her former husband (1956-1961) [Lucien Morisse](link_50), with whom she was on good terms, committed suicide, shooting himself in the head. In April 1975, her close friend singer [Mike Brant](link_51) leapt to his death from an apartment in Paris. He was 28. In July 1983, her lover from 1972 to 1981, [Richard Chanfray](link_52), committed suicide by inhaling the exhaust gas of his Renault 25 car.     
*   She recorded 500 French songs, 200 of which were translated into Italian, and 200 into other languages. She sold more than 80 million records world-wide.     
*   In 1967 her lover, singer [Luigi Tenco](link_49), took his own life. She discovered his dead body. She herself attempted suicide a few days later.     
*   Had been [Richard Chanfray](link_52)'s lover for 9 years. He committed suicide in 1983, three years after they broke up.     
*   She's portrayed by [Sabrina Ferilli](link_53) in [Dalida (2005)](link_54).     
*   Buried in the Montmartre Cemetery, Paris, France.     
*   She received more than 70 gold records and was the first singer to receive platinum and diamond discs.     
*   In 1997, the corner of the rue Girardon and rue de l'Abreuvoir in Montmartre, Paris, was inaugurated as Place Dalida and a large bust in her memory was erected.     
*   Was Miss Egypt 1954 before becoming an international singer     
*   Older sister of [Orlando](link_55) (Bruno Gigliotti), who became her career manager and kept on taking care of her estate, legacy and legendary fame after her suicide.     
*   Was [Joan Collins](link_56) stand-in in [Land of the Pharaohs (1955)](link_57), shot in Egypt at the time she was trying to make her name as an actress.     
*   Twice honoured with the Oscar mondial du succès du disque (the "World Oscar of Recording Success"), she is the only European singer to have won this award more than once.     
*   In December 1967, just after her first suicide attempt, she became pregnant by a 22-year-old Italian student, Lucio. Her decision to have an abortion left her infertile.     
*   Lived with [Jean Sobieski](link_58), [Leelee Sobieski](link_59)'s father, in Paris in the 1960s.     
*   She sold more than 170 million albums worldwide.     
*   In 1987, Dalida was honoured with a commemorative coin minted by The French Mint, Monnaie de Paris, issued in gold, bronze and silver, bearing her likeness.     
*   On the night of 2-3 May 1987, Dalida died by suicide by overdosing on barbiturates. She left behind a note which read, "La vie m'est insupportable. Pardonnez-moi." ("Life is unbearable for me. Forgive me.").     
*   In 2019, she was featured as a Google Doodle on what would have been her 86th birthday.     
*   In 1988, a Encyclopædia Universalis poll, published in the French newspaper Le Monde placed Dalida as second in personalities who had the greatest impact on French society, behind Général de Gaulle.     
*   She is a gay icon in France and the Middle East.     
*   Came from a very Catholic Italian family.

We are constantly working to enhance the user experience for both contributors and readers, improve site security, and ensure reliable access to our websites globally. This infrastructure and product support sustain one of the top ten most visited websites in the world, all at a fraction of the cost of popular for-profit websites.

French singer [Dalida](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dalida "Dalida") signed a recording contract with [Barclay](link_3), a label owned by [Eddie Barclay](link_4), in 1956. In late 1960s, her brother Orlando became her producer which resulted signing recording contract with [Orlando Productions](link_5) in 1970.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dalida_discography#cite_note-1) Under those two recording houses, she recorded up to 700 songs in 9 different languages and in her name was released more than 500 different records in various [audio formats](link_6), accumulatively during and after her life.

This list contains solely the releases issued during Dalida's life. Her albums, singles and EPs are listed below and organised by type and chronology. The titles are taken from the covers, or title songs, or if the title of one song is larger than the others. Some albums are commonly named. In other countries Dalida has released the same records whose [cover art](link_7) was frequently different, and sometimes the tracks names were translated to languages of countries of release. Those records are not specifically highlighted as they are merely variations of the ones that are listed.

_**Dalida**_ is a 2005 French-Italian two-part television film directed by [Joyce Buñuel](link_3).[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dalida_(2005_film)#cite_note-1) The film is about the life of Italian-French singer and actress [Dalida](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dalida "Dalida").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dalida_(2005_film)#cite_note-2)

## Plot

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Dalida_(2005_film)&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Plot")]

The series deals with French-Italian singer [Dalida](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dalida "Dalida"), from her birth to Italian parents in [Cairo](link_4), [Egypt](link_5), to her long and successful singing career in Europe, Asia, America and Africa, until her tragic death in [Paris](link_6), [France](link_7).

# Ennio Morricone facts for kids

[Kids Encyclopedia Facts](link_0)

| Quick facts for kids Ennio Morricone [OMRI](link_5) |
| --- |
| [![Image 3: Ennio Morricone Cannes 2007.jpg](https://kids.kiddle.co/images/thumb/5/5f/Ennio_Morricone_Cannes_2007.jpg/300px-Ennio_Morricone_Cannes_2007.jpg)](https://kids.kiddle.co/Image:Ennio_Morricone_Cannes_2007.jpg) Morricone in 2007 |
| Background information |
| Birth name | Ennio Morricone |
| Also known as | * Maestro * Dan Savio * Leo Nichols |
| Born | (1928-11-10)10 November 1928 [Rome](link_6), [Kingdom of Italy](link_7) |
| Died | 6 July 2020(2020-07-06) (aged 91) Rome, Italy |
| Genres | * [Film music](link_8) * [classical](link_9) * absolute music * [jazz](link_10) * [pop](link_11) * [rock](link_12) * [avant-garde](link_13) |
| Occupation(s) | * Composer * [orchestrator](link_14) * conductor * musician * producer |
| Instruments | Trumpet, piano |
| Years active | 1946–2020 |
|  |
| Signature |
| [![Image 4: EM-Signature.svg](https://kids.kiddle.co/images/thumb/9/98/EM-Signature.svg/150px-EM-Signature.svg.png)](https://kids.kiddle.co/Image:EM-Signature.svg) |
|  |

**Ennio Morricone** (born November 10, 1928 – died July 6, 2020) was an amazing Italian [composer](link_15). He also worked as an [orchestrator](link_14), [conductor](link_16), [trumpeter](link_17), and [pianist](link_18). He wrote music in many different styles.

Morricone created over 400 [music scores](link_8) for movies and TV shows. He also wrote more than 100 classical pieces. Many people think he was one of the greatest and most active film composers ever. He won many awards. These include two [Academy Awards](link_19), three [Grammy Awards](link_20), and three [Golden Globes](link_21). He also received six [BAFTAs](link_22) and the Polar Music Prize in 2010.

## Contents

*   [Early Life and Music School](https://kids.kiddle.co/Ennio_Morricone#Early_Life_and_Music_School)
*   [Amazing Music Career](https://kids.kiddle.co/Ennio_Morricone#Amazing_Music_Career)
*   [Life Outside Music](https://kids.kiddle.co/Ennio_Morricone#Life_Outside_Music)
*   [Awards and Honors](https://kids.kiddle.co/Ennio_Morricone#Awards_and_Honors)
*   [Images for kids](https://kids.kiddle.co/Ennio_Morricone#Images_for_kids)
*   [See also](https://kids.kiddle.co/Ennio_Morricone#See_also)

## Early Life and Music School

Ennio Morricone was born in [Rome](link_6), Italy. His father, Mario Morricone, was a musician. His mother, Libera Ridolfi, started a small textile business. Ennio had four brothers and sisters. At the time he was born, [Italy](link_23) was under [fascist](link_24) rule.

Ennio's father first taught him how to read music. He also taught him to play several instruments. Ennio went to the Saint Cecilia Conservatory for trumpet lessons. He officially joined the conservatory in 1940 when he was 12 years old. He finished a four-year harmony program in just six months! He studied trumpet, composition, and [choral music](link_25). His main teacher was [Goffredo Petrassi](link_26).

[![Image 5: Goffredo.petrassi2](https://kids.kiddle.co/images/thumb/6/63/Goffredo.petrassi2.jpg/300px-Goffredo.petrassi2.jpg)](https://kids.kiddle.co/Image:Goffredo.petrassi2.jpg)

[](https://kids.kiddle.co/Image:Goffredo.petrassi2.jpg "Enlarge")

[Goffredo Petrassi](link_26), Ennio Morricone's music teacher

In 1941, Ennio was chosen to play in the Orchestra of the Opera. He got his diploma in trumpet in 1946. He kept working on classical music and arrangements. He finished his studies at the Conservatory of Santa Cecilia in 1954.

## Amazing Music Career

Morricone wrote his first music when he was only six years old. People saw his talent and encouraged him to keep going.

In 1953, he started writing music for radio shows. Soon, he began creating music for movies. He composed for more than 70 award-winning films. He worked on all of [Sergio Leone](link_27)'s films, starting with _A Fistful of Dollars_. He also scored all of [Giuseppe Tornatore](link_28)'s films, beginning with _Cinema Paradiso_.

Some of his most famous movie scores include:

*   _The Good, the Bad and the Ugly_ (1966)
*   _The Battle of Algiers_ (1968)
*   _1900_ (1976)
*   _The Thing_ (1982)
*   _The Mission_ (1986)
*   _The Untouchables_ (1987)
*   _The Hateful Eight_ (2016)

His music for _The Good, the Bad and the Ugly_ is one of the most famous movie soundtracks ever. It even joined the Grammy Hall of Fame.

Morricone played trumpet in jazz bands in the 1940s. He later became a music arranger for [RCA Victor](link_29). In 1955, he started writing music for films and theater. He composed for famous singers like [Paul Anka](link_30) and [Andrea Bocelli](link_31).

From 1960 to 1975, Morricone became famous worldwide for his music for [Western](link_32) movies. His score for _Once Upon a Time in the West_ sold over 10 million copies. This makes it one of the best-selling movie scores ever.

He also worked with many famous [Hollywood](link_33) directors. These include [Brian De Palma](link_34), [Oliver Stone](link_35), and [Quentin Tarantino](link_36). His well-known songs include "Se telefonando" and "Gabriel's Oboe". Many artists like [Hans Zimmer](link_37) and [Metallica](link_38) have been influenced by his music.

## Life Outside Music

On October 13, 1956, Morricone married Maria Travia. They met in 1950. Maria wrote words for some of her husband's music, like the Latin texts for _The Mission_. They had four children: Marco, Alessandra, Andrea, and Giovanni. Andrea became a conductor and film composer, just like his father. Ennio and Maria were married for 63 years.

Morricone lived in Italy his whole life. He never wanted to move to Hollywood. He said he was a Christian leftist.

Ennio Morricone loved [chess](link_39). He learned to play when he was 11. Before he became super busy with music, he played in chess tournaments in Rome. He even played against famous chess champions like [Garry Kasparov](link_40) and [Anatoly Karpov](link_41). He once played a draw against [Boris Spassky](link_42), a world champion!

On July 6, 2020, Morricone passed away in Rome at age 91. He died from injuries after a fall.

## Awards and Honors

Morricone was nominated for his first [Academy Award](link_19) in 1979. This was for the music in _Days of Heaven_. He received six more Oscar nominations during his career. In February 2016, he won his first competitive Academy Award for his music in _The Hateful Eight_. He was the oldest person ever to win a competitive Oscar at that time.

In 2007, he received an Academy Honorary Award. This award was given "for his magnificent and multifaceted contributions to the art of film music."

The [American Film Institute](link_43) nominated four of his film scores for a spot in the Top 25 Best American Film Scores of All Time. His music for _The Mission_ was ranked 23rd on this list.

In 2009, his score for _The Good, the Bad, and the Ugly_ was added to the Grammy Hall of Fame. In 2010, he won the Polar Music Prize with singer [Björk](link_44). This is Sweden's biggest music award.

[![Image 6: Per artem ad deum morricone](https://kids.kiddle.co/images/thumb/0/0f/Per_artem_ad_deum_morricone.jpg/300px-Per_artem_ad_deum_morricone.jpg)](https://kids.kiddle.co/Image:Per_artem_ad_deum_morricone.jpg)

[](https://kids.kiddle.co/Image:Per_artem_ad_deum_morricone.jpg "Enlarge")

 Morricone receiving the Per Artem ad Deum Medal in 2012.

By 2016, Morricone had sold over 70 million records worldwide. His achievements include:

*   Two [Academy Awards](link_19) (one competitive, one honorary)
*   Three [Grammy Awards](link_20)
*   Three [Golden Globes](link_21)
*   Six [BAFTAs](link_22)
*   Ten [David di Donatello](link_45) awards
*   Eleven Nastro d'Argento awards
*   Two European Film Awards
*   The [Golden Lion Honorary Award](link_46)
*   The Polar Music Prize in 2010

## From today's featured article

[![Image 6: Pennsylvania State Capitol](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/43/Flying_the_Pride_Flag_over_the_Capitol_%2850035197647%29.jpg/250px-Flying_the_Pride_Flag_over_the_Capitol_%2850035197647%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Flying_the_Pride_Flag_over_the_Capitol_(50035197647).jpg "Pennsylvania State Capitol")

The **[Pennsylvania State Capitol](link_35)** is located in [Harrisburg](link_23). The building was designed by [Joseph Miller Huston](link_24) and completed in 1906 in a [Beaux-Arts](link_25) style with decorative [Renaissance](link_26) themes. It houses the legislative chambers for the [Pennsylvania General Assembly](link_27), the Harrisburg chambers for the [Supreme Court](link_28) and [Superior Court of Pennsylvania](link_29), and the offices of [the state's governor](link_30) and [lieutenant governor](link_31). The capitol project was the subject of a [graft](link_32) scandal, as the construction and furnishing cost three times more than the General Assembly had appropriated for the project. The Pennsylvania State Capitol is often referred to as a "palace of art" because of its many sculptures, murals, and stained-glass windows, most of which are Pennsylvania-themed or were made in Pennsylvania. The building was listed on the [National Register of Historic Places](link_33) in 1977 and designated a [National Historic Landmark](link_34) in 2006. _(**[Full article...](link_35)**)_

*   ... that from 1959 all Guinean people aged 7 to 35 years old statutorily belonged to the **[Youth of the African Democratic Revolution](link_43)**?
*   ... that **[Grady Prestage](link_44)** was the first African American elected to the [Fort Bend County](link_45) commissioners' court since Reconstruction?
*   ... that John James Audubon gave his wife ownership of **[his Manhattan estate](link_46)** to prevent debt collectors from seizing it?
*   ... that **[Philoxenos Yuhanon Dolabani](link_47)** defied church policy against Assyrian nationalism through anonymous poetry?
*   ... that the anthropomorphic skunk **[Sabrina](link_48)** has been called "one of the most famous [furry](link_49) comics stars"?

## [Biography](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0197931/bio/?ref_=nmbio_ov_ql_1#mini_bio)

*   Dalida was a French-Italian singer, born to Italian parents in Egypt. She moved to France in her 30's, where she enjoyed the most successful part of her career. She was born on January 17, 1933 in Cairo, Egypt as Yolande Christina Gigliotti. She was married to Lucien Morisse. She died on May 3, 1987 in Paris, France.

## [Trivia](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0197931/bio/?ref_=nmbio_ov_ql_1#trivia)

*   While Dalida was professionally very successful, her private life was marred by a series of failed relationships and personal problems. In January 1967, Dalida took part in the Sanremo Festival with her new lover, Italian singer, songwriter and actor [Luigi Tenco](link_52). The song he presented was "Ciao amore ciao" ("Bye Love, Bye"), which he sang together with Dalida. But stressed, Tenco failed despite Dalida's performance. Tenco committed suicide on 27 January 1967, after learning that his song had been eliminated from the final competition. Tenco was found by Dalida in his hotel room with a bullet wound in his left temple and a note announcing that his gesture was against the jury and public's choices during the competition. In September 1970 her former husband (1956-1961) [Lucien Morisse](link_53), with whom she was on good terms, committed suicide, shooting himself in the head. In April 1975, her close friend singer [Mike Brant](link_54) leapt to his death from an apartment in Paris. He was 28. In July 1983, her lover from 1972 to 1981, [Richard Chanfray](link_55), committed suicide by inhaling the exhaust gas of his Renault 25 car.   
*   She recorded 500 French songs, 200 of which were translated into Italian, and 200 into other languages. She sold more than 80 million records world-wide.   
*   In 1967 her lover, singer [Luigi Tenco](link_52), took his own life. She discovered his dead body. She herself attempted suicide a few days later.   
*   Had been [Richard Chanfray](link_55)'s lover for 9 years. He committed suicide in 1983, three years after they broke up.   
*   She's portrayed by [Sabrina Ferilli](link_56) in [Dalida (2005)](link_57).   

16 more See all

## [Quotes](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0197931/bio/?ref_=nmbio_ov_ql_1#quotes)

*   My cinematographic experience did not leave me any souvenirs, because I was only in very bad films that no one saw! It was better they didn't! In Europe, it is rare for women singers to be in movies. And then, may be that deep within me I didn't really wished to be in movies, for it is my belief that if I really wanted to, I'd be in the movies. I firmly believe that everybody is able to realise what their wishes, provided that they really want to.

# Apulia facts for kids

[Kids Encyclopedia Facts](https://kids.kiddle.co/)

| Quick facts for kids Apulia _Puglia_ |
| --- |
| [Region of Italy](https://kids.kiddle.co/Regions_of_Italy "Regions of Italy") |
| [![Image 3: Flag of Apulia](https://kids.kiddle.co/images/thumb/b/b8/Flag_of_Apulia.svg/100px-Flag_of_Apulia.svg.png)](https://kids.kiddle.co/Image:Flag_of_Apulia.svg "Flag of Apulia") Flag[![Image 4: Coat of arms of Apulia](https://kids.kiddle.co/images/thumb/d/d0/Coat_of_Arms_of_Apulia.svg/50px-Coat_of_Arms_of_Apulia.svg.png)](https://kids.kiddle.co/Image:Coat_of_Arms_of_Apulia.svg "Coat of arms of Apulia") Coat of arms |

| [Time zone](https://kids.kiddle.co/Time_zone "Time zone") | [UTC+1](https://kids.kiddle.co/UTC%2B1 "UTC+1") ([CET](https://kids.kiddle.co/Central_European_Time "Central European Time")) |
| •Summer ([DST](https://kids.kiddle.co/Daylight_saving_time "Daylight saving time")) | [UTC+2](https://kids.kiddle.co/UTC%2B2 "UTC+2") ([CEST](https://kids.kiddle.co/Central_European_Summer_Time "Central European Summer Time")) |

**Apulia** (called _Puglia_ in Italian) is a beautiful region in southern [Italy](https://kids.kiddle.co/Italy "Italy"). It's located right on the [Adriatic Sea](https://kids.kiddle.co/Adriatic_Sea "Adriatic Sea"). The main city, or [capital](https://kids.kiddle.co/Capital_city "Capital city"), is [Bari](https://kids.kiddle.co/Bari "Bari").

If you look at a map of Italy, Apulia forms the 'heel' of the boot-shaped country. This southernmost part is known as the Salento [peninsula](https://kids.kiddle.co/Peninsula "Peninsula").

## Contents

*   [Apulia's Location and Size](https://kids.kiddle.co/Apulia#Apulia.27s_Location_and_Size)
*   [Provinces of Apulia](https://kids.kiddle.co/Apulia#Provinces_of_Apulia)
*   [Famous Places in Apulia](https://kids.kiddle.co/Apulia#Famous_Places_in_Apulia)
*   [Images for kids](https://kids.kiddle.co/Apulia#Images_for_kids)
*   [See also](https://kids.kiddle.co/Apulia#See_also)

## Apulia's Location and Size

Apulia is found in [Southern Italy](https://kids.kiddle.co/Southern_Italy "Southern Italy"). It covers an area of about 19,451 square kilometers (7,510 square miles). Imagine an area roughly the size of the state of New Jersey in the USA!

Around 4 million people live in Apulia. This means there are about 210 people living in every square kilometer.

The region has many neighbors. To the northwest, it borders [Molise](https://kids.kiddle.co/Molise "Molise"). To the west, you'll find [Campania](https://kids.kiddle.co/Campania "Campania"), and to the southwest, [Basilicata](https://kids.kiddle.co/Basilicata "Basilicata"). The [Adriatic Sea](https://kids.kiddle.co/Adriatic_Sea "Adriatic Sea") is to the north and east. To the southeast, there's the [Strait of Otranto](https://kids.kiddle.co/Strait_of_Otranto "Strait of Otranto") and the [Ionian Sea](https://kids.kiddle.co/Ionian_Sea "Ionian Sea"). The [Gulf of Taranto](https://kids.kiddle.co/Gulf_of_Taranto "Gulf of Taranto") is to the south.

## Provinces of Apulia

Apulia is divided into six smaller areas called [provinces](https://kids.kiddle.co/Provinces_of_Italy "Provinces of Italy"). Think of them like counties or states within a larger region. Each province has its own main city.

[![Image 6: Apulia Provinces](https://kids.kiddle.co/images/thumb/7/7c/Apulia_Provinces.png/400px-Apulia_Provinces.png)](https://kids.kiddle.co/Image:Apulia_Provinces.png)

[](https://kids.kiddle.co/Image:Apulia_Provinces.png "Enlarge")

 A map showing the different provinces within Apulia.

Here are the six provinces:

*   [Bari](https://kids.kiddle.co/Metropolitan_City_of_Bari "Metropolitan City of Bari") (BA)
*   [Barletta-Andria-Trani](https://kids.kiddle.co/Province_of_Barletta-Andria-Trani "Province of Barletta-Andria-Trani") (BT)
*   [Brindisi](https://kids.kiddle.co/Province_of_Brindisi "Province of Brindisi") (BR)
*   [Foggia](https://kids.kiddle.co/Province_of_Foggia "Province of Foggia") (FG)
*   [Lecce](https://kids.kiddle.co/Province_of_Lecce "Province of Lecce") (LE)
*   [Taranto](https://kids.kiddle.co/Province_of_Taranto "Province of Taranto") (TA)

## Famous Places in Apulia

Apulia is home to many interesting and historic places. Some of these are very famous landmarks.

*   [![Image 7: Castel del Monte BW 2016-10-14 12-26-11 r](https://kids.kiddle.co/images/thumb/4/42/Castel_del_Monte_BW_2016-10-14_12-26-11_r.jpg/246px-Castel_del_Monte_BW_2016-10-14_12-26-11_r.jpg)](https://kids.kiddle.co/Image:Castel_del_Monte_BW_2016-10-14_12-26-11_r.jpg)  _Castel del Monte_ in [Andria](https://kids.kiddle.co/Andria "Andria"), a famous castle and symbol of the region.  
*   [![Image 8: Petruzzellibarioggi](https://kids.kiddle.co/images/thumb/c/c8/Petruzzellibarioggi.jpg/240px-Petruzzellibarioggi.jpg)](https://kids.kiddle.co/Image:Petruzzellibarioggi.jpg)  _Teatro Petruzzelli_ in [Bari](https://kids.kiddle.co/Bari "Bari"), a beautiful theater.  
*   [![Image 9: Ostuni](https://kids.kiddle.co/images/thumb/c/c8/Ostuni.jpg/241px-Ostuni.jpg)](https://kids.kiddle.co/Image:Ostuni.jpg)  The [medieval](https://kids.kiddle.co/Middle_Ages "Middle Ages") town of Ostuni, known for its white buildings.  

## Images for kids

*   [![Image 10: Torre Sant'Andrea (Lecce)](https://kids.kiddle.co/images/thumb/4/48/Torre_Sant%27Andrea_%28Lecce%29.jpg/120px-Torre_Sant%27Andrea_%28Lecce%29.jpg)](https://kids.kiddle.co/Image:Torre_Sant%27Andrea_(Lecce).jpg)  Torre Sant'Andrea, a beautiful coastal spot in Salento.  
*   [![Image 11: Murge Castel del Monte](https://kids.kiddle.co/images/thumb/3/31/Murge_Castel_del_Monte.jpg/120px-Murge_Castel_del_Monte.jpg)](https://kids.kiddle.co/Image:Murge_Castel_del_Monte.jpg)  The landscape of the Murge plateau.  
*   [![Image 12: Castel del Monte, Andria](https://kids.kiddle.co/images/thumb/0/08/Castel_del_Monte%2C_Andria.jpg/120px-Castel_del_Monte%2C_Andria.jpg)](https://kids.kiddle.co/Image:Castel_del_Monte,_Andria.jpg)  Castel del Monte, built by [King Frederick II](https://kids.kiddle.co/Frederick_II,_Holy_Roman_Emperor "Frederick II, Holy Roman Emperor") between 1240 and 1250 in [Andria](https://kids.kiddle.co/Andria "Andria").  
*   [![Image 13: Vigneto a tendone in agro di Barletta](https://kids.kiddle.co/images/thumb/4/45/Vigneto_a_tendone_in_agro_di_Barletta.JPG/120px-Vigneto_a_tendone_in_agro_di_Barletta.JPG)](https://kids.kiddle.co/Image:Vigneto_a_tendone_in_agro_di_Barletta.JPG)  An awning vineyard in the countryside near Barletta.  
*   [![Image 14: Terre Tarentine](https://kids.kiddle.co/images/thumb/6/60/Terre_Tarentine.jpg/120px-Terre_Tarentine.jpg)](https://kids.kiddle.co/Image:Terre_Tarentine.jpg)  Olive extra virgin oil from Terre Tarentine.  
*   [![Image 15: Ulivi modugno2](https://kids.kiddle.co/images/thumb/9/9c/Ulivi_modugno2.jpg/120px-Ulivi_modugno2.jpg)](https://kids.kiddle.co/Image:Ulivi_modugno2.jpg)  Olive trees near Modugno.  
*   [![Image 16: Dentex dentex 1](https://kids.kiddle.co/images/thumb/f/f3/Dentex_dentex_1.jpg/120px-Dentex_dentex_1.jpg)](https://kids.kiddle.co/Image:Dentex_dentex_1.jpg)  A Dentex fish.  
*   [![Image 17: Sparus aurata juvenile](https://kids.kiddle.co/images/thumb/0/03/Sparus_aurata_juvenile.jpg/120px-Sparus_aurata_juvenile.jpg)](https://kids.kiddle.co/Image:Sparus_aurata_juvenile.jpg)  A Sea bream fish.  
*   [![Image 18: Pandborealisind](https://kids.kiddle.co/images/thumb/c/c5/Pandborealisind.jpg/120px-Pandborealisind.jpg)](https://kids.kiddle.co/Image:Pandborealisind.jpg)  Shrimp.  
*   [![Image 19: Cozza tarantina](https://kids.kiddle.co/images/thumb/5/54/Cozza_tarantina.jpg/120px-Cozza_tarantina.jpg)](https://kids.kiddle.co/Image:Cozza_tarantina.jpg)  Mussels from Taranto.  
*   [![Image 20: Spaghetti con le cozze 2](https://kids.kiddle.co/images/thumb/0/09/Spaghetti_con_le_cozze_2.jpg/120px-Spaghetti_con_le_cozze_2.jpg)](https://kids.kiddle.co/Image:Spaghetti_con_le_cozze_2.jpg)  Spaghetti with mussels.  
*   [![Image 21: Munaceddhri](https://kids.kiddle.co/images/thumb/2/23/Munaceddhri.jpg/120px-Munaceddhri.jpg)](https://kids.kiddle.co/Image:Munaceddhri.jpg)  Monacelle (a type of land snail).  
*   [![Image 22: La scapece](https://kids.kiddle.co/images/thumb/f/fe/La_scapece.JPG/120px-La_scapece.JPG)](https://kids.kiddle.co/Image:La_scapece.JPG)  Scapece gallipolina: fried fish preserved in red wine vinegar.  
*   [![Image 23: Marro al forno con patate](https://kids.kiddle.co/images/thumb/4/47/Marro_al_forno_con_patate.JPG/107px-Marro_al_forno_con_patate.JPG)](https://kids.kiddle.co/Image:Marro_al_forno_con_patate.JPG)  Cazzomarro: baked rolls made from lamb entrails.  
*   [![Image 24: Goat chops](https://kids.kiddle.co/images/thumb/6/63/Goat_chops.jpg/120px-Goat_chops.jpg)](https://kids.kiddle.co/Image:Goat_chops.jpg)  Goat chops.  
*   [![Image 25: Lampascioni](https://kids.kiddle.co/images/thumb/9/9b/Lampascioni.jpg/120px-Lampascioni.jpg)](https://kids.kiddle.co/Image:Lampascioni.jpg)  _Lampascioni sott'olio_, prepared bulbs of a grape hyacinth preserved in olive oil.

*   While Dalida was professionally very successful, her private life was marred by a series of failed relationships and personal problems. In January 1967, Dalida took part in the Sanremo Festival with her new lover, Italian singer, songwriter and actor [Luigi Tenco](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0854903/?ref_=nmbio_trv). The song he presented was "Ciao amore ciao" ("Bye Love, Bye"), which he sang together with Dalida. But stressed, Tenco failed despite Dalida's performance. Tenco committed suicide on 27 January 1967, after learning that his song had been eliminated from the final competition. Tenco was found by Dalida in his hotel room with a bullet wound in his left temple and a note announcing that his gesture was against the jury and public's choices during the competition. In September 1970 her former husband (1956-1961) [Lucien Morisse](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm1126870/?ref_=nmbio_trv), with whom she was on good terms, committed suicide, shooting himself in the head. # Trivia

## Dalida

*   While Dalida was professionally very successful, her private life was marred by a series of failed relationships and personal problems. In January 1967, Dalida took part in the Sanremo Festival with her new lover, Italian singer, songwriter and actor [Luigi Tenco](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0854903/?ref_=nmtrv_trv). Tenco was found by Dalida in his hotel room with a bullet wound in his left temple and a note announcing that his gesture was against the jury and public's choices during the competition. In September 1970 her former husband (1956-1961) [Lucien Morisse](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm1126870/?ref_=nmtrv_trv), with whom she was on good terms, committed suicide, shooting himself in the head. In April 1975, her close friend singer [Mike Brant](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0105259/?ref_=nmtrv_trv) leapt to his death from an apartment in Paris. He was 28. In July 1983, her lover from 1972 to 1981, [Richard Chanfray](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm1145029/?ref_=nmtrv_trv), committed suicide by inhaling the exhaust gas of his Renault 25 car.     
*   She recorded 500 French songs, 200 of which were translated into Italian, and 200 into other languages. She sold more than 80 million records world-wide.     
*   In 1967 her lover, singer [Luigi Tenco](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0854903/?ref_=nmtrv_trv), took his own life. She discovered his dead body. She herself attempted suicide a few days later.     
*   Had been [Richard Chanfray](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm1145029/?ref_=nmtrv_trv)'s lover for 9 years. He committed suicide in 1983, three years after they broke up.     
*   She's portrayed by [Sabrina Ferilli](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0272677/?ref_=nmtrv_trv) in [Dalida (2005)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0416362/?ref_=nmtrv_trv).     
*   Buried in the Montmartre Cemetery, Paris, France.     
*   She received more than 70 gold records and was the first singer to receive platinum and diamond discs.     
*   In 1997, the corner of the rue Girardon and rue de l'Abreuvoir in Montmartre, Paris, was inaugurated as Place Dalida and a large bust in her memory was erected.     
*   Was Miss Egypt 1954 before becoming an international singer     
*   Older sister of [Orlando](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm1491637/?ref_=nmtrv_trv) (Bruno Gigliotti), who became her career manager and kept on taking care of her estate, legacy and legendary fame after her suicide.     
*   Was [Joan Collins](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0001058/?ref_=nmtrv_trv) stand-in in [Land of the Pharaohs (1955)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0048283/?ref_=nmtrv_trv), shot in Egypt at the time she was trying to make her name as an actress.     
*   Twice honoured with the Oscar mondial du succès du disque (the "World Oscar of Recording Success"), she is the only European singer to have won this award more than once.     
*   In December 1967, just after her first suicide attempt, she became pregnant by a 22-year-old Italian student, Lucio. Her decision to have an abortion left her infertile.     
*   Lived with [Jean Sobieski](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0006964/?ref_=nmtrv_trv), [Leelee Sobieski](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0005447/?ref_=nmtrv_trv)'s father, in Paris in the 1960s.     
*   She sold more than 170 million albums worldwide.     
*   In 1987, Dalida was honoured with a commemorative coin minted by The French Mint, Monnaie de Paris, issued in gold, bronze and silver, bearing her likeness.     
*   On the night of 2-3 May 1987, Dalida died by suicide by overdosing on barbiturates. She left behind a note which read, "La vie m'est insupportable. Pardonnez-moi." ("Life is unbearable for me. Forgive me.").     
*   In 2019, she was featured as a Google Doodle on what would have been her 86th birthday.     
*   In 1988, a Encyclopædia Universalis poll, published in the French newspaper Le Monde placed Dalida as second in personalities who had the greatest impact on French society, behind Général de Gaulle.     
*   She is a gay icon in France and the Middle East.     
*   Came from a very Catholic Italian family.

[IMDbPro Starmeter](https://pro.imdb.com/name/nm0854903/?rf=cons_nm_meter&ref_=cons_nm_meter)[See rank](https://pro.imdb.com/name/nm0854903/?rf=cons_nm_meter&ref_=cons_nm_meter)

![Image 3: Luigi Tenco in La cuccagna (1962)](https://m.media-amazon.com/images/M/MV5BMzAzNjQ1NDItMzRiMS00MGRlLWExYzYtMWQ3ZmYyYjZlNGQ3XkEyXkFqcGc@._V1_QL75_UY207_CR97,0,140,207_.jpg)

[](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0854903/mediaviewer/rm4148258304/?ref_=nm_ov_ph)

[](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0854903/bio/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_sm)

Italian 'cantautore' (singer/songwriter), a romantic icon of the 1960's whose budding career ended in a tragic suicide at the age of twenty-eight. Luigi grew up in Cassine and Ricaldone Marazion (province Alessandria), the offspring of an illegitimate union between his mother Teresa and a man whose name he never learned. The man whose name he bore, Giuseppe Tenco, had died as a result of an accident (apparently, he was kicked in the head by a cow!) before Luigi was born. In 1948, Teresa took her son to Genoa where she opened a liquor store, selling Piedmontese wines. While studying at Andrea Doria High School, Tenco learned to play clarinet and piano (later adding alto sax) and formed a jazz band, the Jelly Roll Morton Boys. This venture only lasted a year, but he went on to assemble other groups: 'I Diavoli del Rock' (1958) (whose theme song he also composed) and 'I Cavalieri' (1959) (which he fronted under the alias 'Gigi Mai'). In 1958, he went on tour through Germany with [Adriano Celentano](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0147983/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk). Having signed a contract with the recording label Ricordi in 1961, Tenco turned out his first single, 'Quando'. He also briefly flirted with film acting and got a small part as a rebellious, introverted youth in Luciano Salce''s [La cuccagna (1962)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0055879/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk), in which he also performed the song "La ballata dell'eroe".  
  
Though frequently hamstrung by censorship from Commitee Rai, Tenco was embraced by the public and emerged over the next five years as one of the most popular romantic balladeers on the Italian music scene, releasing hits like "Notturno Senza Luna" (1961), "Mi sono innamorato di te" (1962), the torch song "Vedrai, Vedrai" (1965) and the hauntingly beautiful "Senza Fine" (1961), written by his one-time friend and collaborator [Gino Paoli](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0660020/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk)). By 1965, now under contract with RCA, he found his career momentarily put on hold when he was conscripted for military service. Released on medical grounds in March 1966, Tenco moved to Rome where he met the Egyptian-Italian singer [Dalida](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0197931/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk) with whom he became romantically involved, prompting a feeding frenzy among the paparazzi. To what extent this was a publicity stunt is unclear, since, at the same time, Tenco conducted various other affairs, even proposing marriage to a girl named Valeria, a university student who was expecting a child by him. Valeria was later hit by a car and lost the child.  
  
Tenco's life had already begun to unravel by then. Suffering from depression, he had begun experimenting with cocktails of LSD and mescaline, taking psychotropic drugs against stage fright, becoming obsessive about collecting and carrying firearms. When his entry for the 1967 San Remo Festival failed to make the finals, Tenco committed suicide by gunshot to the right temple in his hotel room, on January 27. Controversy over his death raged for many years. There were allegations that the original police investigations into his death had been botched, that he had, in fact, been murdered. However, thirty-nine years after his death, the original verdict of suicide was confirmed after an autopsy conducted at the Civil Hospital of Acqui Terme in February 2006.

 #### [1. Willa Fitzgerald](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm2560618/?ref_=sr_t_1) 

    *   Actress
    *   Producer
    *   Soundtrack

[Strange Darling (2023)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt22375054/?ref_=sr_knf_1)

Willa Fitzgerald is an American actress, a native of Nashville, Tennessee, United States. Fitzgerald graduated from the Harpeth Hall School, a private college-preparatory school for girls in Nashville in 2009, then received her BA in theater studies from Yale University in 2013. Her career in films started with the role of Vivian in the film [For the Love of a Dog (2007)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0903831/?ref_=sr) in 2008. She debuted on television in 2013 playing Lola Laffer in [Alpha House (2013)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt3012160/?ref_=sr). On April 23, 2014, it was reported that Fitzgerald had obtained a recurring role in the USA Network series [Royal Pains (2009)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt1319735/?ref_=sr), where she played Emma Miller. She has also appeared as a guest star in [Blue Bloods (2010)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt1595859/?ref_=sr), [The Following (2013)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt2071645/?ref_=sr) and [Gotham (2014)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt3749900/?ref_=sr). Her credits in theater include works such as Couple in the Kitchen, The Private Sector, Cow Play and The Cat and the Canary. In August 2016, she joined the cast of the film Misfortune, which was directed by [Lucky McKee](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm1031246/?ref_=sr) and was released in October 2017 under the title [Blood Money (2017)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt3758852/?ref_=sr). In March 2017, Fitzgerald was cast in a starring role in the Fox television pilot [Behind Enemy Lines (2017)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt6474504/?ref_=sr), playing Navy pilot Roxanne Daly, though Fox passed on the pilot in May 2017. In July 2017, Fitzgerald was cast to play Meg in the miniseries [Little Women (2017)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt6853528/?ref_=sr) based on the book of the same name. In November 2017, she was cast as the lead in E!'s pilot [#Fashionvictim (2018)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt7717320/?ref_=sr) as Anya St. Clair. In December 2017, she was cast to play Kitsey Barbour in the upcoming film [The Goldfinch (2019)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt3864056/?ref_=sr) based on Donna Tartt's Pulitzer Prize-winning book of the same name. Her latest role is in the series [Reacher (2022)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt9288030/?ref_=sr) based on Lee Child's books. Reacher is the top ranking series on Amazon, and it has put a whole new spotlight on Fitzgerald's career.

 #### [2. Jim Carrey](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000120/?ref_=sr_t_2) 

    *   Actor
    *   Writer
    *   Producer

[Ace Ventura: Pet Detective (1994)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0109040/?ref_=sr_knf_2)

Jim Carrey, Canadian-born and a U.S. citizen since 2004, is an actor and producer famous for his rubbery body movements and flexible facial expressions. The two-time Golden Globe-winner rose to fame as a cast member of the Fox sketch comedy [In Living Color (1990)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0098830/?ref_=sr) but leading roles in [Ace Ventura: Pet Detective (1994)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0109040/?ref_=sr), [Dumb and Dumber (1994)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0109686/?ref_=sr) and [The Mask (1994)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0110475/?ref_=sr) established him as a bankable comedy actor.  
  
James Eugene Carrey was born on January 17, 1962 in Newmarket, Ontario, Canada, and is the youngest of four children of Kathleen (Oram), a homemaker, and Percy Carrey, an accountant and jazz musician. The family surname was originally "Carré", and he has French-Canadian, Scottish, and Irish ancestry. Carrey was an incurable extrovert from day one. As a child, he performed constantly, for anyone who would watch, and even mailed his résumé to [The Carol Burnett Show (1967)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0061240/?ref_=sr) at age 10. In junior high, he was granted a few precious minutes at the end of each school day to do stand-up routines for his classmates (provided, of course, that he kept a lid on it the rest of the day).  
  
Carrey's early adolescence took a turn for the tragic, however, when the family was forced to relocate from their cozy town of Newmarket to Scarborough (a Toronto suburb). They all took security and janitorial jobs in the Titan Wheels factory, Jim working 8-hour shifts after school let out (not surprisingly, his grades and morale both suffered). When they finally deserted the factory, the family lived out of a Volkswagen camper van until they could return to Toronto.  
  
Carrey made his stand-up debut in Toronto after his parents and siblings got back on their feet. He made his (reportedly awful) professional stand-up debut at Yuk-Yuk's, one of the many local clubs that would serve as his training ground in the years to come. He dropped out of high school, worked on his celebrity impersonations (among them [Michael Landon](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0001446/?ref_=sr) and [James Stewart](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000071/?ref_=sr)), and in 1979 worked up the nerve to move to Los Angeles. He finessed his way into a regular gig at The Comedy Store, where he impressed [Rodney Dangerfield](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0001098/?ref_=sr) so much that the veteran comic signed him as an opening act for an entire season. During this period Carrey met and married waitress Melissa Womer, with whom he had a daughter (Jane). The couple would later go through a very messy divorce, freeing Carrey up for a brief second marriage to actress [Lauren Holly](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000452/?ref_=sr). Wary of falling into the lounge act lifestyle, Carrey began to look around for other performance outlets. He landed a part as a novice cartoonist in the short-lived sitcom [The Duck Factory (1984)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0086702/?ref_=sr); while the show fell flat, the experience gave Carrey the confidence to pursue acting more vigorously.  
  
Carrey also worked on breaking into film around this time. He scored the male lead in the ill-received [Lauren Hutton](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0001381/?ref_=sr) vehicle [Once Bitten (1985)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0089730/?ref_=sr), and had a supporting role in [Peggy Sue Got Married (1986)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0091738/?ref_=sr), before making a modest splash with his appearance as the alien Wiploc in [Earth Girls Are Easy (1988)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0097257/?ref_=sr). Impressed with Carrey's lunacy, fellow extraterrestrial [Damon Wayans](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0001834/?ref_=sr) made a call to his brother, [Keenen Ivory Wayans](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0005540/?ref_=sr), who was in the process of putting together the sketch comedy show [In Living Color (1990)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0098830/?ref_=sr). Carrey joined the cast and quickly made a name for himself with outrageous acts (one of his most popular characters, psychotic Fire Marshall Bill, was attacked by watchdog groups for dispensing ill- advised safety tips).  
  
Following his time on [In Living Color (1990)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0098830/?ref_=sr), Carrey's transformation from TV goofball to marquee headliner happened within the course of a single year. He opened 1994 with a starring turn in [Ace Ventura: Pet Detective (1994)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0109040/?ref_=sr), a film that cashed in on his extremely physical brand of humor (the character's trademark was talking out his derrière). Next up was the manic superhero movie [The Mask (1994)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0110475/?ref_=sr), which had audiences wondering just how far Carrey's features could stretch.  
  
Finally, in December 1994, he hit theaters as a loveable dolt in the Farrelly brothers' [Dumb and Dumber (1994)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0109686/?ref_=sr) (his first multi-million dollar payday). Now a box-office staple, Carrey brought his manic antics onto the set of [Batman Forever (1995)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0112462/?ref_=sr), replacing [Robin Williams](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000245/?ref_=sr) as The Riddler. He also filmed the follow-up to his breakthrough, [Ace Ventura: When Nature Calls (1995)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0112281/?ref_=sr), and inked a deal with Sony to star in [The Cable Guy (1996)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0115798/?ref_=sr) (replacing [Chris Farley](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000394/?ref_=sr)) for a cool $20 million--at the time, that was the biggest up-front sum that had been offered to any comic actor. The movie turned out to be a disappointment, both critically and financially, but Carrey bounced back the next year with the energetic hit [Liar Liar (1997)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0119528/?ref_=sr). Worried that his comic shtick would soon wear thin, Carrey decided to change course.  
  
In 1998, he traded in the megabucks and silly grins to star in [Peter Weir](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0001837/?ref_=sr)'s [The Truman Show (1998)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0120382/?ref_=sr) playing a naive salesman who discovers that his entire life is the subject of a TV show, Carrey demonstrated an uncharacteristic sincerity that took moviegoers by surprise. He won a Golden Globe for the performance, and fans anticipated an Oscar nomination as well--when it didn't materialize, Carrey lashed out at Academy members for their narrow-minded selection process. Perhaps inspired by the snub, Carrey threw himself into his next role with abandon. After edging out a handful of other hopefuls (including [Edward Norton](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0001570/?ref_=sr)) to play eccentric funnyman [Andy Kaufman](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0001412/?ref_=sr) in [Man on the Moon (1999)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0125664/?ref_=sr), Carrey disappeared into the role, living as Kaufman -- and his blustery alter-ego Tony Clifton -- for months (Carrey even owned Kaufman's bongo drums, which he'd used during his audition for director [Miloš Forman](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0001232/?ref_=sr)). His sometimes uncanny impersonation was rewarded with another Golden Globe, but once again the Academy kept quiet.  
  
An indignant Carrey next reprised his bankable mania for the Farrelly brothers in [Me, Myself & Irene (2000)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0183505/?ref_=sr), playing a state trooper whose Jekyll and Hyde personalities both fall in love with the same woman ([Renée Zellweger](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000250/?ref_=sr)). # Trivia

## Dalida

Edit

*   While Dalida was professionally very successful, her private life was marred by a series of failed relationships and personal problems. In January 1967, Dalida took part in the Sanremo Festival with her new lover, Italian singer, songwriter and actor [Luigi Tenco](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0854903/?ref_=nmtrv_trv). The song he presented was "Ciao amore ciao" ("Bye Love, Bye"), which he sang together with Dalida. But stressed, Tenco failed despite Dalida's performance. Tenco committed suicide on 27 January 1967, after learning that his song had been eliminated from the final competition. Tenco was found by Dalida in his hotel room with a bullet wound in his left temple and a note announcing that his gesture was against the jury and public's choices during the competition. In September 1970 her former husband (1956-1961) [Lucien Morisse](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm1126870/?ref_=nmtrv_trv), with whom she was on good terms, committed suicide, shooting himself in the head. In April 1975, her close friend singer [Mike Brant](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0105259/?ref_=nmtrv_trv) leapt to his death from an apartment in Paris. He was 28. In July 1983, her lover from 1972 to 1981, [Richard Chanfray](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm1145029/?ref_=nmtrv_trv), committed suicide by inhaling the exhaust gas of his Renault 25 car.     
*   She recorded 500 French songs, 200 of which were translated into Italian, and 200 into other languages. She sold more than 80 million records world-wide.     
*   In 1967 her lover, singer [Luigi Tenco](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0854903/?ref_=nmtrv_trv), took his own life. She discovered his dead body. She herself attempted suicide a few days later.     
*   Had been [Richard Chanfray](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm1145029/?ref_=nmtrv_trv)'s lover for 9 years. He committed suicide in 1983, three years after they broke up.     
*   She's portrayed by [Sabrina Ferilli](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0272677/?ref_=nmtrv_trv) in [Dalida (2005)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0416362/?ref_=nmtrv_trv).     
*   Buried in the Montmartre Cemetery, Paris, France.     
*   She received more than 70 gold records and was the first singer to receive platinum and diamond discs.     
*   In 1997, the corner of the rue Girardon and rue de l'Abreuvoir in Montmartre, Paris, was inaugurated as Place Dalida and a large bust in her memory was erected.     
*   Was Miss Egypt 1954 before becoming an international singer     
*   Older sister of [Orlando](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm1491637/?ref_=nmtrv_trv) (Bruno Gigliotti), who became her career manager and kept on taking care of her estate, legacy and legendary fame after her suicide.     
*   Was [Joan Collins](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0001058/?ref_=nmtrv_trv) stand-in in [Land of the Pharaohs (1955)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0048283/?ref_=nmtrv_trv), shot in Egypt at the time she was trying to make her name as an actress.     
*   Twice honoured with the Oscar mondial du succès du disque (the "World Oscar of Recording Success"), she is the only European singer to have won this award more than once.     
*   In December 1967, just after her first suicide attempt, she became pregnant by a 22-year-old Italian student, Lucio. Her decision to have an abortion left her infertile.     
*   Lived with [Jean Sobieski](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0006964/?ref_=nmtrv_trv), [Leelee Sobieski](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0005447/?ref_=nmtrv_trv)'s father, in Paris in the 1960s.     
*   She sold more than 170 million albums worldwide.     
*   In 1987, Dalida was honoured with a commemorative coin minted by The French Mint, Monnaie de Paris, issued in gold, bronze and silver, bearing her likeness.     
*   On the night of 2-3 May 1987, Dalida died by suicide by overdosing on barbiturates. She left behind a note which read, "La vie m'est insupportable. Pardonnez-moi." ("Life is unbearable for me. Forgive me.").     
*   In 2019, she was featured as a Google Doodle on what would have been her 86th birthday.     
*   In 1988, a Encyclopædia Universalis poll, published in the French newspaper Le Monde placed Dalida as second in personalities who had the greatest impact on French society, behind Général de Gaulle.     
*   She is a gay icon in France and the Middle East.     
*   Came from a very Catholic Italian family.

*   Dalida was a French-Italian singer, born to Italian parents in Egypt. She moved to France in her 30's, where she enjoyed the most successful part of her career. She was born on January 17, 1933 in Cairo, Egypt as Yolande Christina Gigliotti. She was married to Lucien Morisse. She died on May 3, 1987 in Paris, France.

## [Trivia](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0197931/bio/?ref_=nm_ov_ql_1#trivia)

*   While Dalida was professionally very successful, her private life was marred by a series of failed relationships and personal problems. In January 1967, Dalida took part in the Sanremo Festival with her new lover, Italian singer, songwriter and actor [Luigi Tenco](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0854903/?ref_=nmbio_trv). The song he presented was "Ciao amore ciao" ("Bye Love, Bye"), which he sang together with Dalida. But stressed, Tenco failed despite Dalida's performance. Tenco committed suicide on 27 January 1967, after learning that his song had been eliminated from the final competition. Tenco was found by Dalida in his hotel room with a bullet wound in his left temple and a note announcing that his gesture was against the jury and public's choices during the competition. In September 1970 her former husband (1956-1961) [Lucien Morisse](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm1126870/?ref_=nmbio_trv), with whom she was on good terms, committed suicide, shooting himself in the head. In April 1975, her close friend singer [Mike Brant](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0105259/?ref_=nmbio_trv) leapt to his death from an apartment in Paris. He was 28. In July 1983, her lover from 1972 to 1981, [Richard Chanfray](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm1145029/?ref_=nmbio_trv), committed suicide by inhaling the exhaust gas of his Renault 25 car.   
*   She recorded 500 French songs, 200 of which were translated into Italian, and 200 into other languages. She sold more than 80 million records world-wide.   
*   In 1967 her lover, singer [Luigi Tenco](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0854903/?ref_=nmbio_trv), took his own life. She discovered his dead body. She herself attempted suicide a few days later.   
*   Had been [Richard Chanfray](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm1145029/?ref_=nmbio_trv)'s lover for 9 years. He committed suicide in 1983, three years after they broke up.   
*   She's portrayed by [Sabrina Ferilli](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0272677/?ref_=nmbio_trv) in [Dalida (2005)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0416362/?ref_=nmbio_trv).

*   My cinematographic experience did not leave me any souvenirs, because I was only in very bad films that no one saw! It was better they didn't! In Europe, it is rare for women singers to be in movies. And then, may be that deep within me I didn't really wished to be in movies, for it is my belief that if I really wanted to, I'd be in the movies. I firmly believe that everybody is able to realise what their wishes, provided that they really want to.

_**Son nom est Dalida**_ (_Her name is Dalida_) is the debut [studio album](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Studio_album "Studio album") by French vocalist [Dalida](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dalida "Dalida"). It was released in December 1956 through [Barclay Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barclay_Records "Barclay Records").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Son_nom_est_Dalida#cite_note-Barclay-1)

The tracks in the album are a mixture of vocally highlighted [pop standards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Traditional_pop "Traditional pop"), of which some are basically inspired by [fado](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fado "Fado") and [flamenco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flamenco "Flamenco") genres.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Son_nom_est_Dalida#cite_note-2)

The album received positive reviews from [music critics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_journalism "Music journalism") upon its release, praising Dalida's passionate performance, and nationally reached commercial success, selling around 20,000 units, bracing Dalida as the highest album seller among French singers of that time.

## Background

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Son_nom_est_Dalida&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Background")]

After signing a recording contract with [Barclay Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barclay_Records "Barclay Records") in May 1956, Dalida went on to release three EPs from August to October; _Madona_, _La violetera_ and _Bambino_ respectively. After two moderately successful records, "[Bambino](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bambino_(song) "Bambino (song)")" made Dalida an overnight star as it was an instant success that eventually became the commercially and critically one of the most successful French recordings of all time.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Son_nom_est_Dalida#cite_note-Barclay-1)

### Recording and release

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Son_nom_est_Dalida&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Recording and release")]

The album was completely recorded in Hoche Studios in Paris, under orchestra conduction of [Raymond Lefèvre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raymond_Lef%C3%A8vre "Raymond Lefèvre") and [Wal-Berg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wal-Berg "Wal-Berg").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Son_nom_est_Dalida#cite_note-3) Due to the success of the song, Bambino was used as the title one, while other tracks were fully taken from Dalida's first two EPs including her first recorded song, "Madona".[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Son_nom_est_Dalida#cite_note-Discogs-4)

_Son nom est Dalida_ was released during December 1956, in 25 cm (10 inch) format under catalog number 80 055.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Son_nom_est_Dalida#cite_note-5) It was intended primary for French market, but its success made Barclay release it in USA, United Kingdom, South Africa and Australia. While the cover art of US release is slightly different in colour tone and is titled as _Elle s'appelle Dalida_ (She's called Dalida),[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Son_nom_est_Dalida#cite_note-6) the cover for other [Anglophone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anglophone "Anglophone") countries is completely different that the French one.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Son_nom_est_Dalida#cite_note-7)

In 2002, [Barclay Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barclay_Records "Barclay Records"), then as part of [Universal Music France](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Universal_Music_Group "Universal Music Group"), reissued the album in original vinyl format, and a digitally remastered version in CD, both with original French cover art and track list.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Son_nom_est_Dalida#cite_note-Discogs-4)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Son_nom_est_Dalida#cite_note-8)

#### Public acclaim and sales

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Son_nom_est_Dalida&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Public acclaim and sales")]

Following its release, _Son nom est Dalida_ received highly positive critical acclaim from major French newspapers like Le Figaro, France-Soir and Le Parisien.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Son_nom_est_Dalida#cite_note-9)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Son_nom_est_Dalida#cite_note-10) Dalida also promoted it during her tour in provinces that ended with her first performance in Olympia on 27 February 1957.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Son_nom_est_Dalida#cite_note-Barclay-1)

Since the French music industry at this time was still in the back, albums weren't covered with charts or record sales track. In early 1959, the latter formed official's disc sellers magazine _Music Hall_ listed album with 19,530 units sold since its release in 1956.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Son_nom_est_Dalida#cite_note-11)

The reissued record sold additional 8,500 copies in period of 2002–05, adding up to total sales that almost reach 30,000 units.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Son_nom_est_Dalida#cite_note-12)

_**Miguel**_ is the second album by [Dalida](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dalida "Dalida"). It contains eight songs, including her big success "Miguel". The songs "Maman, la plus belle du monde", "Quand on n'a que l'amour" and "Tu n'as pas très bon caractère", continue in a more pop style than her first album[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miguel_(album)#cite_note-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miguel_(album)#cite_note-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miguel_(album)#cite_note-3)

Dalida was a French-Italian singer, born to Italian parents in Egypt. She moved to France in her 30's, where she enjoyed the most successful part of her career. She was born on January 17, 1933 in Cairo, Egypt as Yolande Christina Gigliotti. She was married to Lucien Morisse. She died on May 3, 1987 in Paris, France.

# Donate

# Donate to the   
Wikimedia Foundation

### Wikipedia is the world’s largest encyclopedia — and it’s yours! Every donation helps keep Wikipedia free and open for people across the globe.

**Only 2% of Wikipedia readers give, so your donation really counts.**

## Ways to give

![Image 5: Illustration of a smiling woman holding a heart, on a teal circular background.](https://wikimediafoundation.org/wp-content/themes/shiro/assets/src/svg/give-icon-friendship.svg)
### [Give once](https://donate.wikimedia.org/?appeal=WP25&pym_appeal=WP25&wmf_medium=wmfSite&wmf_campaign=giveoncebutton&uselang=en&wmf_source=113)

### [Give monthly](https://wikimediafoundation.org/give/give-monthly/)

## More ways to support our work

### [Give by mail](https://wikimediafoundation.org/give/give-by-mail)

## Already a donor?

Thank you for your generous support. It really makes a difference. For information on how to manage your recurring donation, please click below, or contact [donate@wikimedia.org](mailto:donate@wikimedia.org).

[Manage your donation](https://wikimediafoundation.org/give/manage-your-donation/)

## What your donation makes possible

Wikipedia is not funded through advertising, and we don’t sell your data for profit. Instead, we rely on donors — people who find value in the free knowledge and resources we provide. This means Wikipedia remains neutral, trusted, and free from commercial interests. Watch our video to learn more.

[Video 1](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=1Q8s16b39q8)

## Where your donation goes

Accountability and transparency are core values at the Wikimedia Foundation. We manage funds and resources to ensure that every contribution supports our mission. We have earned the Platinum Seal of Transparency from Candid (formerly GuideStar), and Charity Navigator awarded us its highest rating. You can [read our most recent annual report](https://wikimediafoundation.org/annualreports/current/) for more information about our financial health.

### Investment in Technology 45%

Nearly half of our budget goes toward supporting the technology that powers Wikipedia and other Wikimedia projects. We are constantly working to enhance the user experience for both contributors and readers, improve site security, and ensure reliable access to our websites globally. This infrastructure and product support sustain one of the top ten most visited websites in the world, all at a fraction of the cost of popular for-profit websites.

### Support for Volunteers 32%

The global reach of Wikimedia projects is made possible by the hard work of volunteers from across the globe. We provide grants, legal support, and other resources to help build vibrant volunteer communities. Additionally, we promote community engagement through outreach initiatives and advocate for the growth and protection of free knowledge.

### General and Administrative Expenses 11%

Operational costs are essential for the smooth management and governance of the Wikimedia Foundation. These expenses help us recruit top talent and support staff around the world, empowering them to carry out the mission of the Wikimedia Foundation.

### Allocation to Fundraising Efforts 12%

Donor support is crucial to sustaining Wikipedia and our other free knowledge endeavors. Our team is committed to efficient and effective fundraising throughout the year, ensuring that every contribution helps advance our mission.

* * *

## Thank you

We appreciate each and every person who chooses to become a Wikimedia Foundation donor! You are the key to making this important work possible. Thank you. We also offer a special acknowledgement to our Benefactors — people who give $1,000 or more. We proudly list our [Benefactors here](https://wikimediafoundation.org/give/benefactors/).

“Thank you for your thoughtful approach to technology and for ensuring that people remain at the heart of Wikipedia’s mission.”

## Still have questions?

Please find answers to our most frequently asked questions below. If you’re unable to find what you are looking for there, you can browse our [general FAQs](https://wikimediafoundation.org/who-we-are/frequently-asked-questions/), or get in touch using [donate@wikimedia.org](mailto:donate@wikimedia.org).

### Are my donations tax deductible?

The Wikimedia Foundation has 501(c)(3) tax exempt status in the United States. Our tax-exempt status varies according to the laws of each country. Donations to the Wikimedia Foundation are likely not tax-deductible outside the USA. Please see our [tax deductibility](https://wikimediafoundation.org/give/donor-frequently-asked-questions/#tax-deductibility) page for more details.

### What is your donor privacy policy?

We are committed to protecting the privacy rights of our supporters and will never sell, trade, or rent your nonpublic personal information. Please see our [Donor privacy policy](https://foundation.wikimedia.org/wiki/Donor_privacy_policy) for full details.

### How secure is an online donation?

The Wikimedia Foundation donation pages are extremely secure and powered by [GlobalSign](https://www.globalsign.com/). After clicking on a fundraising banner or following a donation link, the page you’re taken to is on a secured site (https); all information is encrypted and handled following the highest standard of data protection.

We would also like you to know that we neither process nor store credit card details or bank information. Instead, we work closely with third party payment processors affiliated with banks to process donations. Please also note that when you transfer to a partner site – if you are donating via Apple Pay, Google Pay, or PayPal, for example – we do not store your login credentials and the full donation process is done from your account on their secure site.

### How can I update my recurring gift?

You may pause, update, or cancel your recurring donation via your donor portal. [Please click here](https://donorpreferences.wikimedia.org/index.php?title=Special:DonorPortal&wmf_medium=wmfSite&wmf_source=113#/login) to log in with the email address you used to set up your donation.

If you donate by credit/debit card, in some cases credit card processors will notify us when card details (including expiration date) are updated, to ensure the donation is not interrupted. If you have questions about this, please contact your credit card provider for more information.

Please note that if you donate via PayPal, you may need to manage your donation directly via your PayPal account.

If you encounter any issues or have any questions, please reach out to our Donor Relations team at [donate@wikimedia.org](mailto:donate@wikimedia.org) and they will be happy to assist. **Please do not include your credit card number or other financial information when contacting us.**

Due to the volume of inquiries we receive, we use Zendesk as a donor response platform. By emailing [donate@wikimedia.org](mailto:donate@wikimedia.org), you understand that your information will be processed by the Zendesk Group in accordance with Zendesk’s terms. Users from the following countries should consult Section A of Zendesk’s privacy policy for more information about Zendesk’s country-specific practices: Australia, Brazil, Canada, Japan, New Zealand, and Singapore.

[View all frequently asked questions](https://wikimediafoundation.org/give/donor-frequently-asked-questions/)

## Don’t just take our word for it

Accountability and transparency are core values at the Wikimedia Foundation. We have earned the Platinum Seal of Transparency from Candid (Formerly Guidestar), and Charity Navigator has awarded us its highest rating of four stars.

# Order of Merit of the Italian Republic facts for kids

[Kids Encyclopedia Facts](https://kids.kiddle.co/)

| Quick facts for kids Order of Merit of the Italian Republic |
| --- |
| [![Image 3: Stemma OMRI.png](https://kids.kiddle.co/images/thumb/c/cc/Stemma_OMRI.png/130px-Stemma_OMRI.png)](https://kids.kiddle.co/Image:Stemma_OMRI.png) Emblem of the order |

| Post-nominals | OMRI |
