| [![Image 4: Cavaliere OMRI BAR.svg](https://kids.kiddle.co/images/thumb/d/dc/Cavaliere_OMRI_BAR.svg/120px-Cavaliere_OMRI_BAR.svg.png)](https://kids.kiddle.co/Image:Cavaliere_OMRI_BAR.svg) [Ribbon](https://kids.kiddle.co/Ribbon "Ribbon") of the order |

[![Image 5: Ordine al merito della Repubblica Italiana](https://kids.kiddle.co/images/thumb/2/26/Ordine_al_merito_della_Repubblica_Italiana.PNG/300px-Ordine_al_merito_della_Repubblica_Italiana.PNG)](https://kids.kiddle.co/Image:Ordine_al_merito_della_Repubblica_Italiana.PNG)

[](https://kids.kiddle.co/Image:Ordine_al_merito_della_Repubblica_Italiana.PNG "Enlarge")

 Commander's badge with a ribbon bow

The **Order of Merit of the Italian Republic** (in Italian, _Ordine al Merito della Repubblica Italiana_) is Italy's highest award for special achievements. It was created in 1951 by [Luigi Einaudi](https://kids.kiddle.co/Luigi_Einaudi "Luigi Einaudi"), who was the second President of Italy.

This important award is given to people who have done great things for their country. This includes achievements in science, writing, art, business, public service, and helping others. It also honors long and excellent service in both civilian and military jobs. When someone receives this award, they can use the letters **OMRI** after their name.

This new order took the place of older national awards like the Civil Order of Savoy and the Order of the Crown of Italy.

## Contents

*   [How Awards Are Given](https://kids.kiddle.co/Order_of_Merit_of_the_Italian_Republic#How_Awards_Are_Given)
*   [Different Levels of the Order](https://kids.kiddle.co/Order_of_Merit_of_the_Italian_Republic#Different_Levels_of_the_Order)
    *   [Who Receives the Highest Honor?](https://kids.kiddle.co/Order_of_Merit_of_the_Italian_Republic#Who_Receives_the_Highest_Honor.3F)

*   [Wearer's guide](https://kids.kiddle.co/Order_of_Merit_of_the_Italian_Republic#Wearer.27s_guide)
*   [Gallery](https://kids.kiddle.co/Order_of_Merit_of_the_Italian_Republic#Gallery)
*   [See also](https://kids.kiddle.co/Order_of_Merit_of_the_Italian_Republic#See_also)

## How Awards Are Given

Awards are usually given out twice a year. One date is June 2, which is the anniversary of Italy becoming a Republic. The other is December 27, the day the Italian Constitution was officially announced. However, sometimes awards can be given at other times, especially if they are for foreign leaders or for people finishing their service.

The special badge for the order was updated in 2001. On one side, it has the words "Al Merito della Repubblica" (To the Merit of the Republic) around Italy's national symbol. On the other side, it has the Latin phrases "Patriæ Unitati" (for the union of the country) and "Civium Libertati" (for the liberty of the citizens) around the head of _Italia turrita_, a symbol of Italy.

The President of Italy, who is the head of all Italian awards, decides who receives the Order. This is usually done with a suggestion from the Prime Minister. Normally, a person's first award cannot be higher than a Knight. People usually need to be at least 35 years old to receive this honor.

## Different Levels of the Order

The Order of Merit has six different levels, or "grades," that people can receive. Each level has its own special ribbon and badge. Here are the grades and how many people had received them by June 2, 2020:

| [![Image 16: Cavaliere OMRI BAR.svg](https://kids.kiddle.co/images/thumb/d/dc/Cavaliere_OMRI_BAR.svg/80px-Cavaliere_OMRI_BAR.svg.png)](https://kids.kiddle.co/Image:Cavaliere_OMRI_BAR.svg) | [![Image 17: ITA OMRI 2001 Cav BAR.svg](https://kids.kiddle.co/images/thumb/a/aa/ITA_OMRI_2001_Cav_BAR.svg/80px-ITA_OMRI_2001_Cav_BAR.svg.png)](https://kids.kiddle.co/Image:ITA_OMRI_2001_Cav_BAR.svg) | 5th Class / Knight | _Cavaliere Ordine al Merito della Repubblica Italiana_ | 146,390 |

#### Who Receives the Highest Honor?

The highest level, the Knight Grand Cross with Collar, is usually given only to [heads of state](https://kids.kiddle.co/Head_of_state "Head of state") (leaders of countries). Many important people from around the world have received this special award. For example, Queen [Elizabeth II](https://kids.kiddle.co/Elizabeth_II "Elizabeth II") of the United Kingdom received it in 1958. More recently, King [Willem-Alexander of the Netherlands](https://kids.kiddle.co/Willem-Alexander_of_the_Netherlands "Willem-Alexander of the Netherlands") received it in 2017, and King [Charles III](https://kids.kiddle.co/Charles_III "Charles III") of the United Kingdom received it in 2025.

**Ennio Morricone** (nacido en [Roma](https://ninos.kiddle.co/Roma "Roma"), el 10 de noviembre de 1928, y fallecido en Roma el 6 de julio de 2020) fue un famoso [compositor](https://ninos.kiddle.co/Compositor "Compositor") y [director de orquesta](https://ninos.kiddle.co/Director_de_orquesta "Director de orquesta")[italiano](https://ninos.kiddle.co/Italia "Italia"). Es muy conocido por haber creado la [banda sonora](https://ninos.kiddle.co/Banda_sonora "Banda sonora") de más de quinientas [películas](https://ninos.kiddle.co/Pel%C3%ADcula "Película") y [series de televisión](https://ninos.kiddle.co/Serie_de_televisi%C3%B3n "Serie de televisión").

Recibió un Óscar honorífico en 2006. También ganó el [Óscar a la mejor banda sonora](https://ninos.kiddle.co/Anexo:%C3%93scar_a_la_mejor_banda_sonora_original "Anexo:Óscar a la mejor banda sonora original") en 2016 por la película _The Hateful Eight_. Sus obras musicales aparecen en más de veinte películas premiadas. Además, compuso piezas sinfónicas y corales.

Es especialmente famoso por su trabajo en las películas del género _[spaghetti western](https://ninos.kiddle.co/Spaghetti\_western "Spaghetti western")_, junto a su amigo el director [Sergio Leone](https://ninos.kiddle.co/Sergio_Leone "Sergio Leone"). Algunas de estas películas son _Por un puñado de dólares_ (1964), _Per qualche dollaro in più_ (1965) y _[El bueno, el feo y el malo](https://ninos.kiddle.co/Il\_buono,\_il\_brutto,\_il\_cattivo "Il buono, il brutto, il cattivo")_ (1966). Su música también se usó en _C'era una volta il West_ (1968).

Ennio Morricone fue uno de los compositores más versátiles e influyentes del siglo XX. Sus bandas sonoras para películas como _Days of Heaven_ (1978), _La misión_ (1986) y _Cinema Paradiso_ (1988) son consideradas obras maestras.

## Biografía de Ennio Morricone

Ennio Morricone nació en [Roma](https://ninos.kiddle.co/Roma "Roma"). Empezó a tocar la [trompeta](https://ninos.kiddle.co/Trompeta "Trompeta") de niño y a los seis años ya había compuesto su primera pieza musical. Su padre, Mario Morricone, que también era músico, lo inscribió en la Academia Nacional de Santa Cecilia cuando tenía nueve años.

A los doce años, Ennio entró al conservatorio. Allí completó un programa de armonía de cuatro años en solo seis meses. En 1946, obtuvo su diploma de trompeta. Ese mismo año, comenzó a trabajar profesionalmente, componiendo música para _Il Mattino_ (_La mañana_).

Después de graduarse en 1954, Morricone trabajó como "escritor fantasma". Esto significa que componía música para películas, pero otros músicos famosos de la época se llevaban el crédito. Pronto se hizo popular creando música de fondo para programas de radio. Poco después, empezó a trabajar en el [cine](https://ninos.kiddle.co/Cine "Cine").

### Primeros años y colaboraciones

En la década de 1950, Morricone obtuvo un diploma en instrumentación. También recibió un diploma en composición de su maestro, el compositor [Goffredo Petrassi](https://ninos.kiddle.co/Goffredo_Petrassi "Goffredo Petrassi"). En 1955, Morricone comenzó a arreglar la música de otros compositores de cine.

Poco tiempo después, [Sergio Leone](https://ninos.kiddle.co/Sergio_Leone "Sergio Leone"), quien había sido compañero de colegio de Morricone, le pidió que compusiera las [bandas sonoras](https://ninos.kiddle.co/Banda_sonora "Banda sonora") para sus películas. Juntos, cambiaron la forma de ver el [western](https://ninos.kiddle.co/W%C3%A9stern "Wéstern") con la película _Por un puñado de dólares_ (1964). Este estilo se conoció como _[spaghetti western](https://ninos.kiddle.co/Spaghetti\_western "Spaghetti western")_. Continuaron trabajando juntos en películas como _[Il buono, il brutto, il cattivo](https://ninos.kiddle.co/Il\_buono,\_il\_brutto,\_il\_cattivo "Il buono, il brutto, il cattivo")_ (1966) y _Giù la testa_ (1971).

### Éxito internacional y premios

En los años 80 y 90, Morricone siguió componiendo para Leone en películas de otros estilos. Un ejemplo es _Érase una vez en América_ (1984). Muchos consideran esta banda sonora una de las mejores de la [historia del cine](https://ninos.kiddle.co/Historia_del_cine "Historia del cine").

También compuso para otros directores importantes. Entre sus trabajos destacan las bandas sonoras para _La misión_ (1986) de [Roland Joffé](https://ninos.kiddle.co/Roland_Joff%C3%A9 "Roland Joffé"), _Los intocables de Eliot Ness_ (1987) de [Brian De Palma](https://ninos.kiddle.co/Brian_De_Palma "Brian De Palma") y _Cinema Paradiso_ (1988) de [Giuseppe Tornatore](https://ninos.kiddle.co/Giuseppe_Tornatore "Giuseppe Tornatore"). Otras composiciones notables más recientes incluyen las películas _Malèna_ (2000) y _Campos de Esperanza_. En 2005, compuso la música para las películas sobre el Papa Juan Pablo II: _Karol: Un hombre que se hizo Papa_ y _Karol: El Papa, el hombre_.

Morricone recibió muchos premios a lo largo de su carrera. Ganó dos [Premios Grammy](https://ninos.kiddle.co/Premios_Grammy "Premios Grammy"), tres [Globos de Oro](https://ninos.kiddle.co/Premios_Globo_de_Oro "Premios Globo de Oro"), cinco [BAFTA](https://ninos.kiddle.co/Premios_BAFTA "Premios BAFTA"), diez [David de Donatello](https://ninos.kiddle.co/Premio_David_de_Donatello "Premio David de Donatello") y once Nastro d'argento. En 2010, recibió el Premio de Música Polar, considerado el "Nobel de la música".

En 2020, le otorgaron el Premio Princesa de Asturias de las Artes, que compartió con el también compositor [John Williams](https://ninos.kiddle.co/John_Williams_(compositor) "John Williams (compositor)"). En 2006, recibió un Óscar honorífico por su gran aporte a la [música de cine](https://ninos.kiddle.co/M%C3%BAsica_cinematogr%C3%A1fica "Música cinematográfica"). En 2016, ganó el Óscar a la [Mejor banda sonora original](https://ninos.kiddle.co/Anexo:%C3%93scar_a_la_mejor_banda_sonora_original "Anexo:Óscar a la mejor banda sonora original") por _The Hateful Eight_. Fue la persona de mayor edad en ganar en esa categoría. A lo largo de su vida, Morricone vendió más de setenta millones de discos.

Una de sus obras más importantes fue una Misa que compuso en 2014. Fue para celebrar los 200 años de la restauración de la [Compañía de Jesús](https://ninos.kiddle.co/Compa%C3%B1%C3%ADa_de_Jes%C3%BAs "Compañía de Jesús"). Se estrenó en la [Iglesia del Gesù](https://ninos.kiddle.co/Iglesia_del_Ges%C3%B9 "Iglesia del Gesù") el 10 de junio de 2015, en honor al Papa [Francisco](https://ninos.kiddle.co/Francisco_(papa) "Francisco (papa)").

Ennio Morricone falleció en Roma el 6 de julio de 2020. Tenía noventa y un años y murió a causa de complicaciones por una fractura de fémur que sufrió tras una caída en su casa.

Musical artist

**Luigi Tenco** (21 March 1938 – 27 January 1967) was an Italian singer-songwriter. He died on the night of 27 January 1967 after a performance at the [Sanremo Music Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sanremo_Music_Festival_1967 "Sanremo Music Festival 1967"). His death was ruled to be the result of suicide, but even decades later, a plethora of evidence in favor of murder was cause to reopen the investigation twice.

## Biography

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Luigi_Tenco&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Biography")]

Tenco was born in [Cassine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cassine,_Piedmont "Cassine, Piedmont") ([province of Alessandria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Province_of_Alessandria "Province of Alessandria")) in 1938, the son of Teresa Zoccola. He never knew his father. Teresa Zoccola was married to Giuseppe Tenco, and they had a son, Valentino, but the couple eventually separated, and Teresa moved to Cassine. It has been rumoured that Luigi Tenco was the product of an extramarital relationship between his mother and an unidentified man of the Micca family, for whom she worked at the time: potentially the sixteen-year-old son or his father. When Zoccola discovered the pregnancy, she returned to Cassine. The boy was given the name of her husband, Tenco, who died in a work accident while she was several months pregnant.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luigi_Tenco#cite_note-tg24-1)

Tenco spent his childhood in Cassine and [Ricaldone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ricaldone "Ricaldone") until 1948, when he moved to [Liguria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liguria "Liguria"), first to [Nervi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nervi "Nervi") and then to [Genoa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genoa "Genoa"), where his mother had a wine shop called _Enos_ in the quarter of La Foce. He developed an early interest in music, teaching himself to play guitar, clarinet and saxophone. During high school, Tenco founded the [Jelly Roll Morton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jelly_Roll_Morton "Jelly Roll Morton") Boys Jazz band, in which Tenco played the clarinet and [Bruno Lauzi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bruno_Lauzi "Bruno Lauzi"), another singer later to become famous, played [banjo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Banjo "Banjo"). [Gino Paoli](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gino_Paoli "Gino Paoli"), who would become one of Italy's most famous singers and songwriters, also played with Tenco in the band he was later involved in, I Diavoli del Rock (The Rock Devils).[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luigi_Tenco#cite_note-tg24-1)

Tenco made his debut in the world of Italian professional music with the band I Cavalieri (The Knights), which included [Giampiero Reverberi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gian_Piero_Reverberi "Gian Piero Reverberi") and [Enzo Jannacci](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Enzo_Jannacci "Enzo Jannacci") amongst others. During this period, he used the pseudonym Gigi Mai. In 1961, Tenco released his first single under his real name, entitled _Quando_ ("When").

He started university studying [electronic engineering](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electronic_engineering "Electronic engineering"), trying to comply with the wishes of his mother and brother. He twice failed the Analytic and Projective Geometry exam (a course he took with professor [Eugenio Giuseppe Togliatti](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eugenio_Giuseppe_Togliatti "Eugenio Giuseppe Togliatti"), the elder brother of Communist party leader [Palmiro Togliatti](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palmiro_Togliatti "Palmiro Togliatti")). Later, he was enrolled in [political science](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Political_science "Political science"), where he gave only two exams.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luigi_Tenco#cite_note-tg24-1)

Tenco was interested in cinema and videomaking. In 1962, he began a short-lived cinematic experience, with [Luciano Salce](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luciano_Salce "Luciano Salce")'s movie _[La Cuccagna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A\_Girl...\_and\_a\_Million "A Girl... and a Million")_. He also collaborated on the soundtrack of the film, and introduced his friend [Fabrizio De André](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fabrizio_De_Andr%C3%A9 "Fabrizio De André") (unknown at the time) through the song _La ballata dell'eroe_ (_Ballad for a hero_).[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luigi_Tenco#cite_note-2) Director [Luigi Comencini](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luigi_Comencini "Luigi Comencini") considered Tenco for the role of Bube in his film _[La ragazza di Bube](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La\_ragazza\_di\_Bube\_(film) "La ragazza di Bube (film)")_, based on [Carlo Cassola](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carlo_Cassola "Carlo Cassola")'s novel. **Rome** (in [Italian](https://kids.kiddle.co/Italian_language "Italian language") and [Latin](https://kids.kiddle.co/Latin "Latin"): _Roma_) is the [capital city](https://kids.kiddle.co/Capital_city "Capital city") of [Italy](https://kids.kiddle.co/Italy "Italy"). It is also the main city of the [Lazio](https://kids.kiddle.co/Lazio "Lazio") region. Rome has been a big city for nearly 3,000 years.

It is Italy's most populated city, with over 2.8 million people. It is also the third most populated city in the [European Union](https://kids.kiddle.co/European_Union "European Union"). Rome is the center of the Metropolitan City of Rome, which has over 4.3 million people.

Rome is in the middle of Italy, along the [Tiber River](https://kids.kiddle.co/Tiber_River "Tiber River"). [Vatican City](https://kids.kiddle.co/Vatican_City "Vatican City"), the world's smallest country, is located inside Rome. This makes Rome unique, as it is a capital city that contains another country.

Rome's long history goes back 28 centuries. Ancient stories say Rome was founded around 753 BC. However, people lived there much earlier. This makes Rome one of Europe's oldest cities where people have lived continuously.

![Image 24](https://kids.kiddle.co/images/thumb/a/ad/Flag_of_Italy_%281861-1946%29.svg/23px-Flag_of_Italy_%281861-1946%29.svg.png)[Kingdom of Italy](https://kids.kiddle.co/Italy "Italy") 1870–1946  
![Image 25](https://kids.kiddle.co/images/thumb/0/00/Flag_of_the_Vatican_City.svg/15px-Flag_of_the_Vatican_City.svg.png)[Vatican City](https://kids.kiddle.co/Vatican_City "Vatican City") 1929–present  
![Image 26](https://kids.kiddle.co/images/thumb/0/03/Flag_of_Italy.svg/23px-Flag_of_Italy.svg.png)[Italian Republic](https://kids.kiddle.co/Italy "Italy") 1946–present

No one knows for sure how [ancient Rome](https://kids.kiddle.co/Ancient_Rome "Ancient Rome") was founded. A popular [myth](https://kids.kiddle.co/Mythology "Mythology") tells the story of twin brothers, [Romulus and Remus](https://kids.kiddle.co/Romulus_and_Remus "Romulus and Remus"). They were said to be raised by a she-[wolf](https://kids.kiddle.co/Wolf "Wolf"). Romulus killed Remus and became the first king of Rome. There is no historical proof for this story, but it is still very famous.

### From Kingdom to Republic

After the [Roman Kingdom](https://kids.kiddle.co/Roman_Kingdom "Roman Kingdom") ended, the [Roman Republic](https://kids.kiddle.co/Roman_Republic "Roman Republic") began. The new Republic fought and took over lands around it. In [390 BC](https://kids.kiddle.co/390_BC "390 BC"), the city was attacked by [Gauls](https://kids.kiddle.co/Gaul "Gaul"). Later, Rome fought against [Carthage](https://kids.kiddle.co/Carthage "Carthage") in big wars. The Roman army won and destroyed Carthage.

### The Rise of Emperors

Rome grew a lot under [Julius Caesar](https://kids.kiddle.co/Julius_Caesar "Julius Caesar") in the first century BC. His adopted son, [Augustus](https://kids.kiddle.co/Augustus "Augustus"), became the first emperor. Augustus famously said he "found a city of bricks and left it of [marble](https://kids.kiddle.co/Marble "Marble")". Later emperors added many new buildings, temples, and arches.

### Decline and Papal Rule

As the [Roman Empire](https://kids.kiddle.co/Roman_Empire "Roman Empire") weakened, Rome became less important. The city fell into ruin. The [pope](https://kids.kiddle.co/Pope "Pope") then began to rule Rome. It became the capital of the [Papal States](https://kids.kiddle.co/Papal_States "Papal States"), which lasted until the 1800s. Popes, like emperors, became very rich. Rome was called the "capital of [Christendom](https://kids.kiddle.co/Christendom "Christendom")" because it was home to important churches.

In 1870, [Giuseppe Garibaldi](https://kids.kiddle.co/Giuseppe_Garibaldi "Giuseppe Garibaldi")'s army united Italy. They entered Rome, and the city became the capital of the new Italian state.

## Rome Today

Rome is a major European center for politics and culture. It is home to the [FAO](https://kids.kiddle.co/Food_and_Agriculture_Organization "Food and Agriculture Organization"), a part of the [United Nations](https://kids.kiddle.co/United_Nations "United Nations"). Rome was one of the most powerful cities in the ancient world. Today, it has many [museums](https://kids.kiddle.co/Museum "Museum"), churches, and [palaces](https://kids.kiddle.co/Palace "Palace"), like the famous [Colosseum](https://kids.kiddle.co/Colosseum "Colosseum").

## Rome's Geography

[![Image 27: Rome, Italy](https://kids.kiddle.co/images/thumb/5/5f/Rome%2C_Italy.JPG/300px-Rome%2C_Italy.JPG)](https://kids.kiddle.co/Image:Rome,_Italy.JPG)

[](https://kids.kiddle.co/Image:Rome,_Italy.JPG "Enlarge")

 Astronaut view of Rome, 2002

### Where is Rome Located?

Rome is in the [Lazio](https://kids.kiddle.co/Lazio "Lazio") region of [central Italy](https://kids.kiddle.co/Central_Italy "Central Italy"). It sits on the [Tiber River](https://kids.kiddle.co/Tiber_River "Tiber River"). The first settlement grew on hills near a shallow part of the river. The old city of Rome was built on seven hills: the Aventine Hill, Caelian Hill, [Capitoline Hill](https://kids.kiddle.co/Capitoline_Hill "Capitoline Hill"), Esquiline Hill, [Palatine Hill](https://kids.kiddle.co/Palatine_Hill "Palatine Hill"), Quirinal Hill, and Viminal Hill. _**Alarms in the Heart**_ is the second and final studio album by English folk rock band [Dry the River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dry_the_River "Dry the River"). It was released on 25 August 2014 through [Transgressive Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transgressive_Records "Transgressive Records"). Partially recorded during a stay at an isolated studio in [Iceland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iceland "Iceland"), the album features collaborations with Scottish singer-songwriter [Emma Pollock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emma_Pollock "Emma Pollock") and Icelandic producer [Valgeir Sigurðsson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Valgeir_Sigur%C3%B0sson "Valgeir Sigurðsson"). _Alarms in the Heart_ produced three singles and was supported by a twelve-date UK tour in 2015.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alarms_in_the_Heart#cite_note-DIY_roller-1) The band broke up in November 2015 after releasing _Hooves of Doubt_, an EP of songs recorded during _Alarms in the Heart_'s Icelandic recording sessions.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alarms_in_the_Heart#cite_note-DIY_EP-2)

## Background and recording

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Alarms_in_the_Heart&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Background and recording")]

After three years of heavy touring following their debut album _[Shallow Bed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shallow\_Bed "Shallow Bed")_, the band chose to record _Alarms in the Heart_ at [Sundlaugin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sundlaugin "Sundlaugin")[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alarms_in_the_Heart#cite_note-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alarms_in_the_Heart#cite_note-4), an isolated studio in Iceland near the city of [Reykjavík](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reykjav%C3%ADk "Reykjavík").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alarms_in_the_Heart#cite_note-icenews-5) During their Iceland sessions, the band worked with producer [Charlie Hugall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlie_Hugall "Charlie Hugall") and received string arrangements from Icelandic producer [Valgeir Sigurðsson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Valgeir_Sigur%C3%B0sson "Valgeir Sigurðsson").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alarms_in_the_Heart#cite_note-soundsphere-6) The band would later use extra songs recorded in Iceland for their final EP _Hooves of Doubt_ in November 2015.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alarms_in_the_Heart#cite_note-DIY_EP-2)

To promote the album, the band released a 10-minute documentary film, titled _Alarms in the Heart (The Making Of)_, which chronicles the album's recording and the band's stay in Iceland. Brice Ezell of _[PopMatters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PopMatters "PopMatters")_ praised the film as "gorgeously shot" and called the scenery of Iceland "particularly stunning".[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alarms_in_the_Heart#cite_note-7)

The band continued recording in their home city of London as they were unsatisfied with the results of the recording sessions in Iceland. During this time, they were dropped by their label, [RCA Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RCA_Records "RCA Records"), which guitarist Matthew Taylor said was a "blessing in disguise" as it allowed them more time to finish _Alarms in the Heart_. Recording continued with Hugall and [Peter Miles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Miles_(music_producer) "Peter Miles (music producer)"), with the band also visiting [Glasgow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glasgow "Glasgow") to work with producer [Paul Savage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Savage_(musician) "Paul Savage (musician)").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alarms_in_the_Heart#cite_note-soundsphere-6) Violinist and founding band member Will Harvey parted ways with the band during the production of the album; Taylor stated that it was due to the band using more keyboards compared to their prior acoustic-focused sound.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alarms_in_the_Heart#cite_note-DIY_interview-8) Only Harvey's contributions to the track "Vessel" made it onto the final album.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alarms_in_the_Heart#cite_note-liner_notes-9)

The first single for _Alarms in the Heart_, "Gethsemane", was released on 16 June 2014 alongside a music video and the announcement of the album. The song's music video was filmed at the [Rivoli Ballroom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rivoli_Ballroom "Rivoli Ballroom") in London, England.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alarms_in_the_Heart#cite_note-10) The second single, "Everlasting Light", was released on 23 July 2014 with a music video directed by Jake Dypka.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alarms_in_the_Heart#cite_note-11) A third and final single, "Rollerskate", was released on 9 March 2015 with a live music video of their performance at [The Forum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/O2_Forum_Kentish_Town "O2 Forum Kentish Town") in London.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alarms_in_the_Heart#cite_note-DIY_roller-1)

## Composition

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Alarms_in_the_Heart&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Composition")]

_Alarms in the Heart_ has been described as an [indie rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indie_rock "Indie rock")[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alarms_in_the_Heart#cite_note-soundsphere-6) and [folk rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Folk_rock "Folk rock")[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alarms_in_the_Heart#cite_note-DIY-12) record. Multiple critics felt it was stylistically similar to the band's previous album, _Shallow Bed_.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alarms_in_the_Heart#cite_note-BestFit-13)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alarms_in_the_Heart#cite_note-wnyc-14) James Christopher Monger of [AllMusic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AllMusic "AllMusic") called the album a "blend [of] the bucolic [art-pop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Art_pop "Art pop") of [Stornoway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stornoway_(band) "Stornoway (band)") with the ceiling-peeling [arena rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arena_rock "Arena rock") of [The Killers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Killers "The Killers")."[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alarms_in_the_Heart#cite_note-AM-15) Michael Katzif of [WNYC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WNYC "WNYC") said "_Alarms In The Heart_ further showcases Dry the River’s skill in building quaint, folk hymnals into a chest-thumping choruses and elegant [Baroque pop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baroque_pop "Baroque pop") songs into impassioned cascading showstoppers."[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alarms_in_the_Heart#cite_note-wnyc-14)

The band's songwriter, Peter Liddle, said the album is divided between the slower and more atmospheric songs they recorded in Iceland and the more "visceral" songs they recorded in London.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alarms_in_the_Heart#cite_note-icenews-5) Meggie Morris of _[Renowned for Sound](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Renowned\_for\_Sound "Renowned for Sound")_ noted the frequent religious themes in the music, calling the lyrics "immersed in the Catholic liturgical and musical tradition" and comparing the melodies on the album to [modal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gregorian_mode "Gregorian mode")[Gregorian chants](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gregorian_chant "Gregorian chant").[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alarms_in_the_Heart#cite_note-16) The album's third track, "Roman Candle", features vocals from Scottish singer-songwriter [Emma Pollock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emma_Pollock "Emma Pollock") as the band felt it was "a little much" to have Liddle perform the entire song.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alarms_in_the_Heart#cite_note-soundsphere-6)

## Critical reception

## M ind-blowing F acts

[![Image 5: Pillars of creation 2014 HST WFC3-UVIS full-res denoised](https://kids.kiddle.co/images/thumb/6/68/Pillars_of_creation_2014_HST_WFC3-UVIS_full-res_denoised.jpg/300px-Pillars_of_creation_2014_HST_WFC3-UVIS_full-res_denoised.jpg)](https://kids.kiddle.co/Image:Pillars_of_creation_2014_HST_WFC3-UVIS_full-res_denoised.jpg)

[](https://kids.kiddle.co/Image:Pillars_of_creation_2014_HST_WFC3-UVIS_full-res_denoised.jpg "Enlarge")

 The Pillars of Creation in the [Eagle Nebula](https://kids.kiddle.co/Eagle_Nebula "Eagle Nebula"), one of the most famous space photographs in history taken by the Hubble Space Telescope.

**When the [Hubble Space Telescope](https://kids.kiddle.co/Hubble_Space_Telescope "Hubble Space Telescope") first opened its robotic eyes in 1990, scientists were shocked to see that every picture came out blurry.**

What had gone wrong? Hubble's giant main mirror had been polished into the wrong shape by a mistake smaller than 1/50th the thickness of a human hair! That tiny error was too small to see, but it was big enough to keep light from focusing correctly.

 Thankfully, astronomers and engineers did not give up. In December 1993, a brave crew of astronauts flew into space aboard the [Space Shuttle Endeavour](https://kids.kiddle.co/Space_Shuttle_Endeavour "Space Shuttle Endeavour") on a daring repair mission. During five intense spacewalks, they installed a special tool called COSTAR, which stands for Corrective Optics Space Telescope Axial Replacement. COSTAR worked like a pair of high-tech eyeglasses for Hubble, fixing its blurry vision. When Hubble looked back at the stars, everything was perfectly clear!

 #### [1. Michael Caine](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000323/?ref_=sr_t_1) 

    *   Actor
    *   Producer
    *   Additional Crew

[Youth (2015)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt3312830/?ref_=sr_knf_1)

Sir Michael Caine, originally Maurice Joseph Micklewhite, was raised in London by his parents, Ellen (née Burchell), a cook, and Maurice Micklewhite Sr., a fish-market porter. He had a younger brother, [Stanley Caine](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0129010/?ref_=sr), and an older maternal half-brother named David Burchell. He left school at age 15 and took a series of working-class jobs before joining the British army and serving in Korea during the Korean War, where he saw combat. Upon his return to England, he gravitated toward the theater and got a job as an assistant stage manager. He adopted the name of Caine on the advice of his agent, taking it from a marquee that advertised [The Caine Mutiny (1954)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0046816/?ref_=sr). In the years that followed, he worked in more than 100 television dramas, with repertory companies throughout England and eventually in the stage hit "The Long and the Short and the Tall".  
  
[Zulu (1964)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0058777/?ref_=sr), the epic retelling of a historic 19th-century battle in South Africa between British soldiers and Zulu warriors, brought Caine to international attention. Instead of being typecast as a low-ranking Cockney soldier, he played a snobbish, aristocratic officer. Although "Zulu" was a major success, it was the role of Harry Palmer in [The Ipcress File (1965)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0059319/?ref_=sr) and the title role in [Alfie (1966)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0060086/?ref_=sr) that made Caine a star of the first magnitude. He epitomized the new breed of actor in mid-1960s England, the working-class bloke with glasses and a down-home accent. However, after initially starring in some excellent films, particularly in the 1960s, including [Gambit (1966)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0060445/?ref_=sr), [Funeral in Berlin (1966)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0060437/?ref_=sr), [Play Dirty (1969)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0063443/?ref_=sr), [Battle of Britain (1969)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0064072/?ref_=sr), [Too Late the Hero (1970)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0066471/?ref_=sr), [The Last Valley (1971)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0065969/?ref_=sr) and especially [Get Carter (1971)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0067128/?ref_=sr), he seemed to take on roles in below-average films, simply for the money he could by then command.  
  
However, there were some gems among the dross. He gave a magnificent performance opposite [Sean Connery](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000125/?ref_=sr) in [The Man Who Would Be King (1975)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0073341/?ref_=sr) and turned in a solid one as a German colonel in [The Eagle Has Landed (1976)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0074452/?ref_=sr). [Educating Rita (1983)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0085478/?ref_=sr), [Blame It on Rio (1984)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0086973/?ref_=sr) and [Hannah and Her Sisters (1986)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0091167/?ref_=sr) (for which he won his first Oscar) were highlights of the 1980s, while more recently [Little Voice (1998)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0147004/?ref_=sr), [The Cider House Rules (1999)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0124315/?ref_=sr) (his second Oscar) and [Last Orders (2001)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0253200/?ref_=sr) have been widely acclaimed. Caine played Nigel Powers in the parody sequel [Austin Powers in Goldmember (2002)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0295178/?ref_=sr), and Alfred Pennyworth in [Christopher Nolan](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0634240/?ref_=sr)'s Dark Knight trilogy. He appeared in several other of Nolan's films including [The Prestige (2006)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0482571/?ref_=sr), [Inception (2010)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt1375666/?ref_=sr) and [Interstellar (2014)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0816692/?ref_=sr). He also appeared as a supporting character in [Alfonso Cuarón](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0190859/?ref_=sr)'s [Children of Men (2006)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0206634/?ref_=sr) and Pixar's sequel [Cars 2 (2011)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt1216475/?ref_=sr).  
  
As of 2015, films in which Caine has starred have grossed over $7.4 billion worldwide. He is ranked the ninth highest grossing box office star. Caine is one of several actors nominated for an Academy Award for acting every decade from five consecutive decades (the other being [Laurence Olivier](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000059/?ref_=sr) and [Meryl Streep](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000658/?ref_=sr)). He was appointed Commander of the Order of the British Empire in the 1992 Birthday Honours, and was knighted by Queen Elizabeth II in the 2000 Birthday Honours in recognition for his contributions to the cinema.  
  
Caine has been married twice. First to actress [Patricia Haines](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0354273/?ref_=sr) from 1954 to 1958. They had a daughter, Dominique, in 1957. A bachelor for some dozen-plus years after the divorce, he was romantically linked to [Edina Ronay](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0739914/?ref_=sr) (for three years), [Elizabeth Ercy](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0258716/?ref_=sr), [Nancy Sinatra](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0005434/?ref_=sr), [Natalie Wood](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000081/?ref_=sr), [Candice Bergen](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000298/?ref_=sr), [Bianca Jagger](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0415588/?ref_=sr), [Françoise Pascal](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0664256/?ref_=sr) and [Jill St. John](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0001762/?ref_=sr). In 1971 he met his second wife, fashion model [Shakira Caine](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0129008/?ref_=sr) (née Baksh), and they married in 1973, six months before their daughter Natasha was born. The couple has three grandchildren, and in 2023, they celebrated their 50th wedding anniversary.

When he was 11, he wanted to be a comedian like [Sid Caesar](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0128377/?ref_=sr). Then, when he was 15 and saw [Lee J. Cobb](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0002011/?ref_=sr) in 'Death of a Salesman,' he decided he would be a comedy actor and found that [Mel Brooks](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000316/?ref_=sr) was a great influence on his screen writing. He combined both talents with directing in [The World's Greatest Lover (1977)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0076933/?ref_=sr), followed by [The Adventure of Sherlock Holmes' Smarter Brother (1975)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0072608/?ref_=sr).

 #### [3. Roman Polanski](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000591/?ref_=sr_t_3) 

    *   Director
    *   Actor
    *   Writer

[Chinatown (1974)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0071315/?ref_=sr_knf_3)

Roman Polanski is a Polish film director, producer, writer and actor. Having made films in Poland, Britain, France and the USA, he is considered one of the few truly international filmmakers. Roman Polanski was born in Paris in 1933.  
  
His parents returned to Poland from France in 1936, three years before World War II began. On Germany's invasion in 1939, as a family of mostly Jewish heritage, they were all sent to the Krakow ghetto. His parents were then captured and sent to two different concentration camps: His father to Mauthausen-Gusen in Austria, where he survived the war, and his mother to Auschwitz where she was murdered. Roman witnessed his father's capture and then, at only 7, managed to escape the ghetto and survive the war, at first wandering through the Polish countryside and pretending to be a Roman-Catholic kid visiting his relatives. Although this saved his life, he was severely mistreated suffering nearly fatal beating which left him with a fractured skull.  
  
Local people usually ignored the cinemas where German films were shown, but Polanski seemed little concerned by the propaganda and often went to the movies. As the war progressed, Poland became increasingly war-torn and he lived his life as a tramp, hiding in barns and forests, eating whatever he could steal or find. Still under 12 years old, he encountered some Nazi soldiers who forced him to hold targets while they shot at them. At the war's end in 1945, he reunited with his father who sent him to a technical school, but young Polanski seemed to have already chosen another career. In the 1950s, he took up acting, appearing in [Andrzej Wajda](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0906667/?ref_=sr)'s [A Generation (1955)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0048500/?ref_=sr) before studying at the Lodz Film School. His early shorts such as [Two Men and a Wardrobe (1958)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0051566/?ref_=sr), [Le gros et le maigre (1961)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0054946/?ref_=sr) and [Mammals (1962)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0056521/?ref_=sr), showed his taste for black humor and interest in bizarre human relationships. His feature debut, [Knife in the Water (1962)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0056291/?ref_=sr), was one of the first Polish post-war films not associated with the war theme. It was also the first movie from Poland to get an Oscar nomination for best foreign film. Though already a major Polish filmmaker, Polanski chose to leave the country and headed to France. While down-and-out in Paris, he befriended young scriptwriter, [Gérard Brach](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0102722/?ref_=sr), who eventually became his long-time collaborator. The next two films, [Repulsion (1965)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0059646/?ref_=sr) and [Cul-de-sac (1966)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0060268/?ref_=sr), made in England and co-written by Brach, won respectively Silver and then Golden Bear awards at the Berlin International Film Festival. In 1968, Polanski went to Hollywood, where he made the psychological thriller, [Rosemary's Baby (1968)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0063522/?ref_=sr). However, after the brutal murder of his wife, [Sharon Tate](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0001790/?ref_=sr), by the Manson Family in 1969, the director decided to return to Europe. In 1974, he again made a US release - it was [Chinatown (1974)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0071315/?ref_=sr).  
  
It seemed the beginning of a promising Hollywood career, but after his conviction for the sodomy of a 13-year old girl, Polanski fled from he USA to avoid prison. After [Tess (1979)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0080009/?ref_=sr), which was awarded several Oscars and Cesars, his works in 1980s and 1990s became intermittent and rarely approached the caliber of his earlier films. It wasn't until [The Pianist (2002)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0253474/?ref_=sr) that Polanski came back to full form. French singer [Dalida](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dalida "Dalida") signed a recording contract with [Barclay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barclay_(record_label) "Barclay (record label)"), a label owned by [Eddie Barclay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eddie_Barclay "Eddie Barclay"), in 1956. In late 1960s, her brother Orlando became her producer which resulted signing recording contract with [Orlando Productions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orlando_Productions "Orlando Productions") in 1970.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amore_scusami_(Dalida_album)#cite_note-1) Under those two recording houses, she recorded up to 700 songs in 9 different languages and in her name was released more than 500 different records in various [audio formats](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Audio_formats "Audio formats"), accumulatively during and after her life.

This list contains solely the releases issued during Dalida's life. Her albums, singles and EPs are listed below and organised by type and chronology. The titles are taken from the covers, or title songs, or if the title of one song is larger than the others. Some albums are commonly named. In other countries Dalida has released the same records whose [cover art](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cover_art "Cover art") was frequently different, and sometimes the tracks names were translated to languages of countries of release. Those records are not specifically highlighted as they are merely variations of the ones that are listed.

## From today's featured article

[![Image 4: Pennsylvania State Capitol](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/43/Flying_the_Pride_Flag_over_the_Capitol_%2850035197647%29.jpg/250px-Flying_the_Pride_Flag_over_the_Capitol_%2850035197647%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Flying_the_Pride_Flag_over_the_Capitol_(50035197647).jpg "Pennsylvania State Capitol")

The **[Pennsylvania State Capitol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pennsylvania_State_Capitol "Pennsylvania State Capitol")** is located in [Harrisburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harrisburg,_Pennsylvania "Harrisburg, Pennsylvania"). The building was designed by [Joseph Miller Huston](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joseph_Miller_Huston "Joseph Miller Huston") and completed in 1906 in a [Beaux-Arts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beaux-Arts_architecture "Beaux-Arts architecture") style with decorative [Renaissance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Renaissance_Revival_architecture "Renaissance Revival architecture") themes. It houses the legislative chambers for the [Pennsylvania General Assembly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pennsylvania_General_Assembly "Pennsylvania General Assembly"), the Harrisburg chambers for the [Supreme Court](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Supreme_Court_of_Pennsylvania "Supreme Court of Pennsylvania") and [Superior Court of Pennsylvania](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Superior_Court_of_Pennsylvania "Superior Court of Pennsylvania"), and the offices of [the state's governor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_governors_of_Pennsylvania "List of governors of Pennsylvania") and [lieutenant governor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lieutenant_Governor_of_Pennsylvania "Lieutenant Governor of Pennsylvania"). The capitol project was the subject of a [graft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Graft_(politics) "Graft (politics)") scandal, as the construction and furnishing cost three times more than the General Assembly had appropriated for the project. The Pennsylvania State Capitol is often referred to as a "palace of art" because of its many sculptures, murals, and stained-glass windows, most of which are Pennsylvania-themed or were made in Pennsylvania. The building was listed on the [National Register of Historic Places](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Register_of_Historic_Places "National Register of Historic Places") in 1977 and designated a [National Historic Landmark](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Historic_Landmark "National Historic Landmark") in 2006. _(**[Full article...](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pennsylvania\_State\_Capitol "Pennsylvania State Capitol")**)_

Ernst Frey

*   ... that the melodies of _**[Alarms in the Heart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alarms\_in\_the\_Heart "Alarms in the Heart")**_ were likened to Gregorian chants?
*   ... that Australian model **[Cindy Rostron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cindy_Rostron "Cindy Rostron")** also had a career as an Indigenous ranger?

*   ... that **[Grady Prestage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grady_Prestage "Grady Prestage")** was the first African American elected to the [Fort Bend County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fort_Bend_County,_Texas "Fort Bend County, Texas") commissioners' court since Reconstruction?
*   ... that John James Audubon gave his wife ownership of **[his Manhattan estate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Audubon_Park,_Manhattan "Audubon Park, Manhattan")** to prevent debt collectors from seizing it?
*   ... that **[Philoxenos Yuhanon Dolabani](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philoxenos_Yuhanon_Dolabani "Philoxenos Yuhanon Dolabani")** defied church policy against Assyrian nationalism through anonymous poetry?
*   ... that the anthropomorphic skunk **[Sabrina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sabrina_Online "Sabrina Online")** has been called "one of the most famous [furry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Furry_fandom "Furry fandom") comics stars"?

#### [Excellent movie worth seeing ...](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0416362/reviews/?featured=rw1514029&ref_=tt_ururv_c_1_hd)

I really don't understand why some people were so negative in their appraisal of this movie. I thought it was amazingly well-done, and in fact have watched it numerous times. It got to the point that I was calling friends over and forcing them to watch it with me, which I normally never do for a movie! In short, the acting was sensational ... you really feel for Ferilli as she's portraying all the twists and turns in Dalida's life. As for the moving being two fast ... it's a woman's entire life in two DVDs!! Be reasonable ... how much do you expect them to be able to fit in? Anyway, I say "Excellent Work!" and ... when is it coming out on DVD in North America? ;)

#### [Better than the 2016 film](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0416362/reviews/?featured=rw5665364&ref_=tt_ururv_c_2_hd)

I prefer this one over the 2016 film which in my opinion was too shallow, confusing, and directed in a strange way which omitted too many important details, while giving often biased views of her life.  
  
This 2-part TV film however also omits a large part of Dalida's life (the first 22 years of her life in Cairo, Egypt) where she was born and participated in several activities including her 1955 Miss Egypt Beauty Pageant which led her to participate in several Egyptian movies, until finally a French director discovered her while filming The Mask of Tutankamoun in Luxor, and persuaded her to try her luck singing in France.  
  
Seems like both directors of this movie and the 2016 one don't want to show any details about her 22 years of living in Egypt. What a shame since she was already well-known in Egypt before moving to France and becoming an international star there. I'm sure a lot of fans would have liked to see what life in Egypt was like back in the 1950's-quite a modern, cosmopolitan, prosperous place to be full of people from different parts of the world including other Italians like Dalida's family, Greeks, Armenians, British, and even French.

#### [One good scene](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0416362/reviews/?featured=rw1568553&ref_=tt_ururv_c_3_hd)

One good scene-the suicide scene, she made it look so beautiful. You are right who ever you are when you said that the actress was a far cry from Dalida but she did give it her best and you get some sense of this beautiful lovely creature that went by too fast like a comet and died. The early Egyptian scenes were interesting and I LOVED the scene in her home town that portrayed all her neighbors and friends dancing to a small 45 player on the unpaved streets of that suburb. The long dialog scenes were a bit of a drag and I wish they would have shown her winning Miss Egypt in 1955 which is the event that propelled her to Europe and super stardom as well...but if you love Dalida as I do you will love this film. Growing up in Israel in the 60's she dominated the charts and has found a warm cosy corner in my heart Toby Ross

#### [television product](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0416362/reviews/?featured=rw1082662&ref_=tt_ururv_c_4_hd)

I'm a huge (huge, really huge) fan of Dalida. I was waiting with great expectation for this movie. I saw it and couldn't find anywhere the Dalida I "know". Everything is shown in fast forward, one doesn't have time to absorb everything, because suddenly you have a subtitle saying "3 years later". The actress (probably) gave her best, but wasn't enough, even forgetting the physical unresemblance, the fact that she was dubbed doesn't help her much. Couldn't they find someone who speaks french? As Italian was not needed because even with her family or Luigi Tenco, she always spoke in french (odd, don' you think?). But pay close attention to Vittoria Scognamiglio, the french voice of Dalida - it's absolutely unbelievable. She the only thing that's worth on this movie: she managed to get the right tone, accent, color... you seem your listening to Dali's talking. The rest of the cast is average: Arnaud Giovaninetti and Charles Berling are above average. It's a shame that such a great story couldn't be told in another way: with a steady pulse, with passion and not with a soap opera undertone that discarded all possibilities of making something memorable. We'll always have her story...  
  
PartII I've seen a couple of times more these series. Although I still agree with all from the above, I have to admit that some things start to look better: Sabrina Ferilli does a remarkable effort to convey the right feelings from this tormented character. The production valus are outsatnding: sets, props and wardrobe. The choice of the songs and the original soundtrack are great. I guess I really needed to see it once more to start enjoying. I've changed my rating from 3 to 5.

#### [Supremely Superficial Bio of a Supremely Superficial Drama Diva](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0416362/reviews/?featured=rw1562802&ref_=tt_ururv_c_5_hd)

This TV bio is perfectly adapted to its subject: It has the intellectual gravity of a sea cucumber and the superficial good looks of the drama queen it depicts. Dalida's torments were mostly of her own making and the result of egotism, ignorance, narcissism, vanity, hormonal imbalances, greed, possessiveness, shallowness and narrowmindedness. There is no way this film can make them look interesting without resorting to dire soap opera effects, i.e. one surgical emergency after another whenever tension slacks or Dalida's career or chicken-hawk love affairs lapse into repetition. The series furthermore makes no effort to compare Dalida's output with that of her contemporary equals, e.g. Petula Clark et al., to describe her place in the variety firmament or to give a glimpse of the society she moved around in. Supporting roles are equally wasted, hollow and one-dimensional. Strictly for spectators of both sexes who wish to channel their inner drag queen...

## [Trivia](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0197931/bio/?ref_=nmtrv_ov_ql_1#trivia)

*   While Dalida was professionally very successful, her private life was marred by a series of failed relationships and personal problems. In January 1967, Dalida took part in the Sanremo Festival with her new lover, Italian singer, songwriter and actor [Luigi Tenco](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0854903/?ref_=nmbio_trv). The song he presented was "Ciao amore ciao" ("Bye Love, Bye"), which he sang together with Dalida. But stressed, Tenco failed despite Dalida's performance. Tenco committed suicide on 27 January 1967, after learning that his song had been eliminated from the final competition. Tenco was found by Dalida in his hotel room with a bullet wound in his left temple and a note announcing that his gesture was against the jury and public's choices during the competition. In September 1970 her former husband (1956-1961) [Lucien Morisse](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm1126870/?ref_=nmbio_trv), with whom she was on good terms, committed suicide, shooting himself in the head. In April 1975, her close friend singer [Mike Brant](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0105259/?ref_=nmbio_trv) leapt to his death from an apartment in Paris. He was 28. In July 1983, her lover from 1972 to 1981, [Richard Chanfray](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm1145029/?ref_=nmbio_trv), committed suicide by inhaling the exhaust gas of his Renault 25 car.   
*   She recorded 500 French songs, 200 of which were translated into Italian, and 200 into other languages. She sold more than 80 million records world-wide.   
*   In 1967 her lover, singer [Luigi Tenco](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0854903/?ref_=nmbio_trv), took his own life. She discovered his dead body. She herself attempted suicide a few days later.   
*   Had been [Richard Chanfray](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm1145029/?ref_=nmbio_trv)'s lover for 9 years. He committed suicide in 1983, three years after they broke up.   
*   She's portrayed by [Sabrina Ferilli](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0272677/?ref_=nmbio_trv) in [Dalida (2005)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0416362/?ref_=nmbio_trv).

*   My cinematographic experience did not leave me any souvenirs, because I was only in very bad films that no one saw! It was better they didn't! In Europe, it is rare for women singers to be in movies. And then, may be that deep within me I didn't really wished to be in movies, for it is my belief that if I really wanted to, I'd be in the movies. _**Dalida**_ is a 2005 French-Italian two-part television film directed by [Joyce Buñuel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joyce_Bu%C3%B1uel "Joyce Buñuel").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dalida_(2005_film)#cite_note-1) The film is about the life of Italian-French singer and actress [Dalida](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dalida "Dalida").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dalida_(2005_film)#cite_note-2)

## Plot

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Dalida_(2005_film)&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Plot")]

The series deals with French-Italian singer [Dalida](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dalida "Dalida"), from her birth to Italian parents in [Cairo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cairo "Cairo"), [Egypt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Egypt "Egypt"), to her long and successful singing career in Europe, Asia, America and Africa, until her tragic death in [Paris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paris "Paris"), [France](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/France "France").

## [Biography](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0197931/bio/#mini_bio)

*   Dalida was a French-Italian singer, born to Italian parents in Egypt. She moved to France in her 30's, where she enjoyed the most successful part of her career. She was born on January 17, 1933 in Cairo, Egypt as Yolande Christina Gigliotti. She was married to Lucien Morisse. She died on May 3, 1987 in Paris, France.

## [Trivia](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0197931/bio/#trivia)

*   While Dalida was professionally very successful, her private life was marred by a series of failed relationships and personal problems. In January 1967, Dalida took part in the Sanremo Festival with her new lover, Italian singer, songwriter and actor [Luigi Tenco](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0854903/?ref_=nmbio_trv). The song he presented was "Ciao amore ciao" ("Bye Love, Bye"), which he sang together with Dalida. But stressed, Tenco failed despite Dalida's performance. Tenco committed suicide on 27 January 1967, after learning that his song had been eliminated from the final competition. Tenco was found by Dalida in his hotel room with a bullet wound in his left temple and a note announcing that his gesture was against the jury and public's choices during the competition. In September 1970 her former husband (1956-1961) [Lucien Morisse](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm1126870/?ref_=nmbio_trv), with whom she was on good terms, committed suicide, shooting himself in the head. In April 1975, her close friend singer [Mike Brant](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0105259/?ref_=nmbio_trv) leapt to his death from an apartment in Paris. He was 28. In July 1983, her lover from 1972 to 1981, [Richard Chanfray](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm1145029/?ref_=nmbio_trv), committed suicide by inhaling the exhaust gas of his Renault 25 car.   
*   She recorded 500 French songs, 200 of which were translated into Italian, and 200 into other languages. She sold more than 80 million records world-wide.   
*   In 1967 her lover, singer [Luigi Tenco](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0854903/?ref_=nmbio_trv), took his own life. She discovered his dead body. She herself attempted suicide a few days later.   
*   Had been [Richard Chanfray](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm1145029/?ref_=nmbio_trv)'s lover for 9 years. He committed suicide in 1983, three years after they broke up.   
*   She's portrayed by [Sabrina Ferilli](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0272677/?ref_=nmbio_trv) in [Dalida (2005)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0416362/?ref_=nmbio_trv).

## [Trivia](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0197931/bio/?ref_=nmbio_ov_ql_1#trivia)

*   While Dalida was professionally very successful, her private life was marred by a series of failed relationships and personal problems. In January 1967, Dalida took part in the Sanremo Festival with her new lover, Italian singer, songwriter and actor [Luigi Tenco](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0854903/?ref_=nmbio_trv). The song he presented was "Ciao amore ciao" ("Bye Love, Bye"), which he sang together with Dalida. But stressed, Tenco failed despite Dalida's performance. Tenco committed suicide on 27 January 1967, after learning that his song had been eliminated from the final competition. Tenco was found by Dalida in his hotel room with a bullet wound in his left temple and a note announcing that his gesture was against the jury and public's choices during the competition. In September 1970 her former husband (1956-1961) [Lucien Morisse](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm1126870/?ref_=nmbio_trv), with whom she was on good terms, committed suicide, shooting himself in the head. In April 1975, her close friend singer [Mike Brant](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0105259/?ref_=nmbio_trv) leapt to his death from an apartment in Paris. He was 28. In July 1983, her lover from 1972 to 1981, [Richard Chanfray](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm1145029/?ref_=nmbio_trv), committed suicide by inhaling the exhaust gas of his Renault 25 car.   
*   She recorded 500 French songs, 200 of which were translated into Italian, and 200 into other languages. She sold more than 80 million records world-wide.   
*   In 1967 her lover, singer [Luigi Tenco](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0854903/?ref_=nmbio_trv), took his own life. She discovered his dead body. She herself attempted suicide a few days later.   
*   Had been [Richard Chanfray](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm1145029/?ref_=nmbio_trv)'s lover for 9 years. He committed suicide in 1983, three years after they broke up.   
*   She's portrayed by [Sabrina Ferilli](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0272677/?ref_=nmbio_trv) in [Dalida (2005)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0416362/?ref_=nmbio_trv).

## [Trivia](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0197931/bio/?ref_=nm_ov_ql_1#trivia)

*   While Dalida was professionally very successful, her private life was marred by a series of failed relationships and personal problems. In January 1967, Dalida took part in the Sanremo Festival with her new lover, Italian singer, songwriter and actor [Luigi Tenco](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0854903/?ref_=nmbio_trv). The song he presented was "Ciao amore ciao" ("Bye Love, Bye"), which he sang together with Dalida. But stressed, Tenco failed despite Dalida's performance. Tenco committed suicide on 27 January 1967, after learning that his song had been eliminated from the final competition. Tenco was found by Dalida in his hotel room with a bullet wound in his left temple and a note announcing that his gesture was against the jury and public's choices during the competition. In September 1970 her former husband (1956-1961) [Lucien Morisse](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm1126870/?ref_=nmbio_trv), with whom she was on good terms, committed suicide, shooting himself in the head. In April 1975, her close friend singer [Mike Brant](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0105259/?ref_=nmbio_trv) leapt to his death from an apartment in Paris. He was 28. In July 1983, her lover from 1972 to 1981, [Richard Chanfray](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm1145029/?ref_=nmbio_trv), committed suicide by inhaling the exhaust gas of his Renault 25 car.   
*   She recorded 500 French songs, 200 of which were translated into Italian, and 200 into other languages. She sold more than 80 million records world-wide.   
*   In 1967 her lover, singer [Luigi Tenco](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0854903/?ref_=nmbio_trv), took his own life. She discovered his dead body. She herself attempted suicide a few days later.   
*   Had been [Richard Chanfray](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm1145029/?ref_=nmbio_trv)'s lover for 9 years. He committed suicide in 1983, three years after they broke up.   
*   She's portrayed by [Sabrina Ferilli](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0272677/?ref_=nmbio_trv) in [Dalida (2005)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0416362/?ref_=nmbio_trv).

Hollywood is mourning the loss of some of its finest stars.

Below, Page Six remembers the actors, singers and more celebs who died in 2025.

## Isiah Whitlock Jr.

[![Image 11: Isiah Whitlock Jr. poses on the red carpet for "Devil In Disguise: John Wayne Gacy."](https://pagesix.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/3/2025/12/isiah-whitlock-jr-attends-peacocks-113168904.jpg?w=683)135](https://pagesix.com/celebrity-news/celebrity-deaths-2025/# "Open a slideshow of all 135 article images.")

Isiah Whitlock Jr. has died. He was 71 years old. Getty Images

“The Wire” actor Isiah Whitlock Jr. [has died](link_43) at age 71.

Whitlock’s manager, Brian Liebman, announced the sad news via Instagram on Dec. 30, penning: “It is with tremendous sadness that I share the passing of my dear friend and client Isiah Whitlock Jr. If you knew him — you loved him. A brilliant actor and even better person. May his memory forever be a blessing. Our hearts are so broken. He will be very, very missed.”

The actor was best known for roles in “The Wire,” “Veep,” “Your Honor” and “The Residence.”[](link_43)

## Tatiana Schlossberg

[![Image 12: Tatiana Schlossberg speaking into a microphone.](https://pagesix.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/3/2025/12/tatiana-schlossberg-attends-intelligencer-live-116139160_b51576.jpg?w=682)135](https://pagesix.com/celebrity-news/celebrity-deaths-2025/# "Open a slideshow of all 135 article images.")

Caroline Kennedy’s daughter Tatiana Schlossberg died after a battle with leukemia, her family announced on Dec. 30. Getty Images for New York Magazine

Caroline Kennedy’s daughter Tatiana Schlossberg [died after a battle with acute myeloid leukemia](link_44), her family announced on Dec. 30.

She was 35 years old.

“Our beautiful Tatiana passed away this morning,” the JFK Library Foundation, on behalf of Schlossberg’s extended family, announced[via Instagram](link_45). “She will always be in our hearts.”

The message was signed by her family, “George, Edwin and Josephine Moran Ed, Caroline, Jack, Rose and Rory.”

Schlossberg — who shared her diagnosis in an essay for the New Yorker, published in November — was initially diagnosed in May 2024 and had been given just a year to live.

She was married to George Moran and the two shared a 3-year-old son and a 1-year-old daughter.

## Melanie Watson Bernhardt

[![Image 13: Melanie Watson as Kathy Gordon in a wheelchair and Gary Coleman as Arnold Jackson on the floor in "Diff'rent Strokes."](https://pagesix.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/3/2025/12/l-r-melanie-watson-kathy-117967197.jpg)135](https://pagesix.com/celebrity-news/celebrity-deaths-2025/# "Open a slideshow of all 135 article images.")

Melanie Watson Bernhardt died at the age of 57. NBCUniversal via Getty Images

Melanie Watson Bernhardt, best known for playing the character Kathy Gordon on”Diff’rent Strokes,” [died Dec. 26](link_46). She was 57.

The actress, who battled the genetic disorder osteogenesis imperfecta — which causes bones to break easily, poor muscle tone, hearing loss, and dental problems — had been hospitalized after suffering bleeding issues, the outlet reported.

Her health reportedly deteriorated quickly after she was hospitalized.

## Brigitte Bardot

[![Image 14: Publicity portrait of French actress Brigitte Bardot.](https://pagesix.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/3/2025/12/publicity-portrait-french-actress-brigitte-117944078_d7c617.jpg)135](https://pagesix.com/celebrity-news/celebrity-deaths-2025/# "Open a slideshow of all 135 article images.")

Brigitte Bardot died on Dec. 28. Getty Images

Brigitte Bardot, the French actress who was named the original “sex kitten,”[has died](link_47), according to her foundation. She was 91.

“The Brigitte Bardot Foundation announces with immense sadness the death of its founder and president, Madame Brigitte Bardot, a world-renowned actress and singer, who chose to abandon her prestigious career to dedicate her life and energy to animal welfare and her foundation,” the foundation, which fights to protect animals,[announced on its website](link_48)Dec. 28.

“The Brigitte Bardot Foundation wishes to honor the memory of an exceptional woman who gave everything for a world more respectful of animals,” it added.

## Mickey Lee

[![Image 15: Mickey Lee, a houseguest on Big Brother season 27, wearing a pink dress.](https://pagesix.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/3/2025/12/mickey-lee-houseguest-season-27-117765520_195ff1.jpg?w=731)135](https://pagesix.com/celebrity-news/celebrity-deaths-2025/# "Open a slideshow of all 135 article images.")

CBS via Getty Images

“Big Brother” Season 51 star Mickey Lee [died on Christmas Day](link_49) after [suffering multiple cardiac arrests](link_50). She was 35.

“Mickey’s light, legacy and impact will never be forgotten,” the reality star’s family members wrote in a lengthy social media statement on Dec. 26.

Earlier that same week, a GoFundMe page dedicated to Lee’s recovery revealed she was in “critical but stable condition” after the “sudden health crisis” with a “long and challenging … road ahead.”

## James Ronsone

[![Image 16: James Ransone, dressed in a black jacket and black pants, stands for a photo at Build Studio.](https://pagesix.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/3/2025/12/james-ransone-discusses-chapter-2-117708022.jpg?w=683)135](https://pagesix.com/celebrity-news/celebrity-deaths-2025/# "Open a slideshow of all 135 article images.")

Getty Images

James Ransone, who played Ziggy on “The Wire,” [died by suicide](link_51) on Dec. 19 at age 46.

The late actor’s widow, Jamie McPhee, [mourned him in a touching Instagram statement](link_52) two days later.

“I told you I have loved you 1000 times before and I know I will love you again,” she wrote. “You told me – I need to be more like you and you need to be more like me – and you were so right. Thank you for giving me the greatest gifts – you, Jack and Violet. We are forever.”

The couple wed in 2017 and shared two children.

Former NASCAR driver Greg Biffle, his wife, Cristina Grossu Biffle, and their two children have died in a plane crash. Instagram/Christina Biffle

Former NASCAR driver Greg Biffle and his wife, Cristina Grossu Biffle, died alongside their two children in a North Carolina plane crash on Dec. 18.

The family’s private jet was trying to land at Statesville Regional Airport around 10:15 a.m. when the accident happened.

The couple was with their 5-year-old son, Ryde, and Biffle’s daughter, Emma, 14, whom he shared with his ex-wife, Nicole Lunders.

Other victims included Dennis Dutton and his son Jack, and Craig Wadsworth.

[![Image 18: Anthony Geary at the 2012 Disney ABC Television TCA summer press tour party.](https://pagesix.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/3/2025/12/2012-disney-abc-television-tca-117394479.jpg?w=728)135](https://pagesix.com/celebrity-news/celebrity-deaths-2025/# "Open a slideshow of all 135 article images.")

“General Hospital” legend Anthony Geary died on Dec. 14. He was 78 years old.

He passed away following complications from an operation three days prior,[TV Insider reported](link_53).

“It was a shock for me and our families and our friends,” Geary’s husband, Claudio Gama, told the outlet in a statement. “For more than 30 years, Tony has been my friend, my companion, my husband.”

He was best known for playing Luke Spencer in the soap opera and appeared in the series from 1978 to 2015.

## Rachael Carpani

[![Image 19: Rachael Carpani as Detective Lina Flores in "Against the Wall."](https://pagesix.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/3/2025/12/season-1-ep-110-117381433.jpg?w=681)135](https://pagesix.com/celebrity-news/celebrity-deaths-2025/# "Open a slideshow of all 135 article images.")

Australian actress Rachael Carpani died. She was 45 years old. ©Lifetime Television/Courtesy Everett Collection

Australian actress Rachael Carpani died. She was 45 years old.

On Dec. 15, her sister announced her death [via Instagram](link_54), sharing that she had passed away following a chronic illness.

“It is with great sadness that Tony and Gael Carpani announce that their beautiful daughter, beloved Australian actress Rachael Carpani, unexpectedly but peacefully passed away after a long battle with chronic illness, in the early hours of Sunday 7th December,” the statement read.

“The family requests privacy at this very difficult time and will be making no further statements,” it concluded.

Carpani was best known for her role as Jodi Fountain in the Australian series“McLeod’s Daughters,”but also acted in“N.C.I.S: Los Angeles.”

R&B singer Carl Carlton died. He was 72 years old. WireImage

Singer Carl Carlton, who is best known for his songs “She’s a Bad Mama Jama” and “Everlasting Love,” died. He was 72 years old.

On Dec. 14,Carlton’s son Carlton Hudgens II [announced on Facebook](link_55)that his father, born Carlton Hudgens, had passed away.

“​​RIP Dad,Legend Carl Carlton, singer of ‘She’s a Bad Mama Jama,” he wrote alongside a photo of the late musician. “Long hard fight in life and you will be missed.”

## 28 décembre 2025

# Décès de notre Fondatrice et Présidente, Madame Brigitte Bardot

![Image 3](https://www.fondationbrigittebardot.fr/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/Banniere-site.jpg)

### Décès de notre Fondatrice et Présidente, Madame Brigitte Bardot

La Fondation Brigitte Bardot annonce avec une immense tristesse, le décès de sa Fondatrice et Présidente, Madame Brigitte Bardot, actrice et chanteuse mondialement reconnue, qui a choisi d’abandonner sa carrière prestigieuse pour dédier sa vie et son énergie à la défense des animaux et à sa Fondation.

En 1962, alors qu’elle n’a que 28 ans, Brigitte Bardot marque les esprits en participant à l’émission emblématique « 5 colonnes à la une » pour exiger l’étourdissement des animaux avant leur abattage, montrant ainsi son engagement précoce.  
Véritable précurseur, elle renonce à 39 ans aux feux de la rampe et au monde artistique pour mettre sa notoriété et toute sa détermination au service des animaux et des êtres les plus faibles, comme les personnes âgées.  
Elle se rend sur la banquise en 1977 afin de venir en aide aux bébés phoques, acte emblématique de son combat pour la protection des espèces vulnérables.  
Sous son impulsion, la Fondation Brigitte Bardot, créée en 1986, devient un acteur majeur de la protection animale en France et dans le Monde entier. Quarante ans après, elle compte plus de12.000 animaux recueillis dans l’«Arche de BB», des actions dans 70 pays, 4 refuges, 300 salariés, des centaines de bénévoles et 40.000 donateurs.  
En interpellant fréquemment les politiques pour faire avancer les législations, en faisant condamner les auteurs de maltraitances, en réalisant chaque jour des sauvetages, en sensibilisant un large public, la Fondation est à son tour considérée comme une référence mondiale dont Brigitte Bardot a veillé à assurer la pérennité.  
La Fondation Brigitte Bardot tient à saluer la mémoire d’une femme exceptionnelle qui a tout donné et tout abandonné pour un monde plus respectueux des animaux. Son héritage demeure vivant à travers les actions et les combats que la Fondation poursuit avec la même passion et la même fidélité à ses idéaux.  
Nous adressons nos sincères condoléances à sa famille, à ses proches, à la municipalité de Saint-Tropez et aux Tropéziens, et à tous ceux qui partagent ce combat.  
La Fondation continuera, plus que jamais, à porter l’œuvre de Brigitte Bardot.

Nos animaliers au sein de nos refuges de [Bazoches](link_24), [La Mare Auzou](link_25), [La Davière](link_26) et [Montpon](link_27) ont voulu rendre eux-aussi hommage à Brigitte Bardot. Présents tous les jours auprès des animaux, ils incarnent la combat de Brigitte au quotidien.

Entourés des animaux qu’elle a toujours défendus, les animaliers de nos refuges disent merci à Brigitte : « Son combat vit en nous, et nous le poursuivrons sans relâche, pour eux, pour elle, pour toujours… Reposez-vous maintenant, on prend le relais… »

Découvrez leur hommage en vidéo.

# Brigitte Bardot, French actress dubbed the original ‘sex kitten,’ dead at 91

 By 

[Tamantha Ryan](link_43)

 Published Dec. 28, 2025, 9:37 a.m. ET

23 23 Comments

See more of our coverage in your search results.

 Make Page Six a Preferred Source 

Brigitte Bardot, the French actress who was named the original “sex kitten,” [has died](https://pagesix.com/celebrity-news/celebrity-deaths-2025/), according to her foundation. She was 91.

“The Brigitte Bardot Foundation announces with immense sadness the death of its founder and president, Madame Brigitte Bardot, a world-renowned actress and singer, who chose to abandon her prestigious career to dedicate her life and energy to animal welfare and her foundation,” the foundation, which fights to protect animals, [announced on its website](https://www.fondationbrigittebardot.fr/deces-de-notre-fondatrice-et-presidente-madame-brigitte-bardot/) Sunday.

“The Brigitte Bardot Foundation wishes to honor the memory of an exceptional woman who gave everything for a world more respectful of animals,” it added.

[![Image 10: Publicity portrait of French actress Brigitte Bardot.](https://pagesix.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/3/2025/12/publicity-portrait-french-actress-brigitte-117944078.jpg)7](https://pagesix.com/2025/12/28/celebrity-news/brigitte-bardot-dead-at-91/# "Open a slideshow of all 7 article images.")

Brigitte Bardot, the French actress who was named the original “sex kitten,” has died, according to her foundation. Getty Images

She was 91. AP

“We extend our sincere condolences to her family, loved ones, the municipality of Saint-Tropez and its residents, and all those who share this cause. The Foundation will continue, more than ever, to champion the work of Brigitte Bardot.”

The foundation’s Bruno Jacquelin [told the Associated Press](link_44) that Bardot had been hospitalized last month and that she passed away in her home in Southern France. No funeral or memorial service arrangements have been made.

Bardot’s cause of death was not disclosed.

French President Emmanuel Macron took to X to share a touching tribute to Bardot.

“Her films, her voice, her dazzling glory, her initials, her sorrows, her generous passion for animals, her face that became Marianne, Brigitte Bardot embodied a life of freedom,” Macron [tweeted Sunday](link_45).

“French existence, universal brilliance. She touched us. We mourn a legend of the century,” he added.

Bardot was launched as an international sex symbol in 1956 when she starred as a sexualized teen bride in the movie “And God Created Woman.”

The film, which was directed by her then-husband, Roger Vadim, featured scenes of Bardot dancing on tables naked, marking a groundbreaking portrayal of female sexuality during a conservative time.

[![Image 17: French actress Brigitte Bardot sitting in a chair, wearing a sheer, sequined top and skirt.](https://pagesix.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/3/2025/12/french-actress-brigitte-bardot-attends-117940763.jpg)7](https://pagesix.com/2025/12/28/celebrity-news/brigitte-bardot-dead-at-91/# "Open a slideshow of all 7 article images.")

After starring in nearly 30 films, she retired from acting in 1973. FilmPublicityArchive/United Archives via Getty Images

[![Image 19: Former French actress Brigitte Bardot displays a 1969 copy of French magazine "Paris Match" showing a seal on the cover.](https://pagesix.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/3/2025/12/1969-copy-french-magazine-paris-117940687.jpg)7](https://pagesix.com/2025/12/28/celebrity-news/brigitte-bardot-dead-at-91/# "Open a slideshow of all 7 article images.")

A decade later, she reemerged as an animal rights lobbyist. REUTERS

After starring in nearly 30 films, Bardot retired from acting in 1973.

A decade later, she reemerged as an animal rights lobbyist and started her animal rights foundation after selling movie memorabilia and jewelry.

Bardot is survived by her fourth husband,Bernard d’Ormale, her estranged son,Nicolas-Jacques Charrier, and her sister.
